- **Approach**: `scripts/hooks/lib/usage_log.py`, `hm_escape.py` and `hm_shape.py` ported onto the guard's `shared/` (the new `shared::usage`, the one writer of `.git/tool-usage.jsonl`; `shared::escape`, the reasons' floor; `shared::shape` and `shared::wait`, ported at T003 and T009), with two gate commands for the shell and Python callers (`l7r-gate log usage|goals`, `l7r-gate escape reason-ok`); every caller repointed; the three and `hm_tree.py`, which nothing ran, deleted in the same cut: before the cut only comments (`main_tree_hooks.rs`, `shared/tree.rs`, two lines of `house_style_cases.rs`) and one recorded command in `tests/hooks/fixtures/guard-refusals-2026-09.json` named it, no script, recipe, hook or module (observed 2026-11-12, method: `git grep -n hm_tree HEAD` over the Makefile, `*.mk`, `*.sh`, `*.py`, `*.rs`, `.claude/` and `tests/`), its port the guard's `shared::tree` since T010.

   **Decisions** (FR-001, FR-002, FR-003, `ask:449-usage-text`, `ask:449-phase3-remainder`):
   - Where it lives: the guard crate's `shared/`, which the gate builds on and the guards cannot reach past, so the gate's writers (`stamp::record_for`, `land`, `speckit-todo`, `ledger-owed`, `planhold-restore`) and the clone-sync guard call one `shared::usage::record` in process, where `stamp.rs` and `checks/passes.rs` each formatted their own line. The commands sit under the gate's `log` (beside `run` and `bypass`) and a new `escape` verb.
   - The callers: the Makefile's `LOGESCAPE`, `idle-tests` and its parse-time goals line, the five `*-gate.sh`, `one-gate.sh`, `sync-with-main.sh` (three places) and `land-tooling.sh` (two) run the gate commands; `clone_sync_hooks.rs` records in process; `memo_check.py`, `phase_sources.py`, `check-entry-headings.py` and `tick-task.py`, which stay Python, run `log usage` by command once after their work, where they imported it, and `escape_log.py` runs `escape reason-ok` once a call. `guardlog.sh`'s `escape_or_refuse` and `guard_cmd` are deleted, not repointed: nothing called either once every guard was Rust (observed 2026-11-12, method: `git grep` of both names). `hm_shape` gets no command: its one outside caller, a no-poll suite case, became a unit test of `shared::wait` that checks the same condition, the escaped wait it builds parsing under `bash -n`.
   - The usage writer appends one line in one write in append mode and takes no `flock`, where the Python took an exclusive one: the Rust writers it replaces already wrote so (HEAD's `tree/src/stamp.rs`, "one write of one short line in append mode", and `shared/checks/passes.rs`), landed and reviewed, and a single append-mode write of a short line is not interleaved by another on a local file; a lock would cost every `make` a process (`File::lock` needs Rust 1.89, the toolchain is 1.87, and the crate's lock helper starts `flock`).
   - `escape::enough` now splits words on Python's whitespace (`\x1c`-`\x1f` included, as `re.split` does), moving every guard toward the Python at the one edge the floor could differ; `reason-ok` reads stdin as this container's `C.UTF-8` Python did (`surrogateescape`, a byte not UTF-8 one character).
   - `check tool-signals` also reads `log usage` as a tool's record marker, skips Rust test files (their fixtures name scratch tools) and names the command in its fix; every registered tool is still found (observed 2026-11-12, method: `scripts/gates/l7r-gate.sh check tool-signals`, exit 0 on the working tree, its suite green in `make hooks-test HOOKS_ALL=1`). Two defects fixed on the way: `test-gate-write-hooks.sh` copied a `preflight.py` that no longer exists, and clone-sync's context carried a `python` field nothing read once the run was in process.
   - The same outputs (FR-002): HEAD's Python from a detached worktree against the Rust, each case set up identically, exit, stdout, stderr and every file in the case's repositories compared: 7,854 cases, none differing, 399 failing on both sides (observed 2026-11-12, method: `/tmp/claude-1000/-diagram/d2dc8c63-4103-4cf9-bc83-e73a2fae792a/scratchpad/t129/diff.py`, `results.json`). Among them 24 argument forms of `record` in three directories and three session values, every argparse refusal, `goals` with up to four goals, three unwritable logs, the 287 tool, kind and outcome triples `.git/tool-usage.jsonl` holds, 6,383 reasons to `reason-ok` (scratch edges, 3,825 real escape reasons from the guard log, every bypass record's `why`, the bash-parse corpus), the gates' and `LOGESCAPE`'s two stdin forms, `escape_log.escape()` end to end (240), and every caller's line as written (observed 2026-11-12, method: the same harness). Normalizations: a usage line's and a guard-log entry's `utc`, the entry's file name, argparse's own text where both exit 2, `--help`, a traceback's text.
   - Timing: the cases took 172.7 s of process time in Python against 81.8 s in Rust (observed 2026-11-12, method: `/tmp/claude-1000/-diagram/d2dc8c63-4103-4cf9-bc83-e73a2fae792a/scratchpad/t129/diff.py`). `make _reference`, which runs the parse-time goals line every `make` pays, 33.0 ms against 16.4 ms, best of nine (observed 2026-11-12, method: `/tmp/claude-1000/-diagram/d2dc8c63-4103-4cf9-bc83-e73a2fae792a/scratchpad/t129/run2.log`). The goals line runs the gate's wrapper with `L7R_GATE_STALE_OK=1`, which runs the binary there is, stale or not, and builds none, building only where there is no binary: without it a `make rust-test` after a gate-crate edit would rebuild the release `l7r-gate` at the Makefile's parse, which `make rust-test` never built before the cut (its recipe runs only `l7r-gate.sh rust`, the separate `l7r-rust` binary T93 made for this loop; `make static`'s already ran `l7r-gate.sh check`), and a stale binary writes the same line. Measured: a one-line edit of the claims crate then `make rust-test CRATE=rust/gate/crates/claims`, three times, 0.61, 0.60 and 0.60 s, `l7r-gate` rebuilt in none (observed 2026-11-12, method: `/tmp/claude-1000/-diagram/d2dc8c63-4103-4cf9-bc83-e73a2fae792a/scratchpad/t129/sc006.sh`, the binary's time before and after each run). A run with no binary at all builds it as before, and one whose build fails records nothing for that run.
   - The census at the cut: provenance comments, the old-form fixtures of `test-check-tool-signals.sh` (still accepted: the word stays a marker the check reads) and `specs/449-rust-codebase/measurements.json`'s `phase-1-python-share`, whose values name the four as a census of 2026-11-08 and whose command runs none of them (observed 2026-11-12, method: `git grep -E "usage_log|hm_escape|hm_shape|hm_tree"`). The checks: `make static` clean on 20 crates, `make rust-test` green (the guard 556 tests, `core` 71, `checks` 101), `make hooks-test HOOKS_ALL=1` green on 54 suites, the pointer check clean (observed 2026-11-12, method: those commands). One `make static` run went red once on `ledger_passes::settle::tests::a_kept_cost_is_served_while_its_transcript_stands` while the harness loaded the machine, green on two reruns and the last run, in code this task did not change (observed 2026-11-12, method: the port's runs), the flake T120 recorded.

### T129 Approach (checklist part A)

1. **The goal, in the world.** The hook libraries are Rust, one writer of the usage log, no Python started on a `make` parse.
2. **The constraints.** FR-001, FR-002 and FR-003, `ask:449-phase3-remainder`.
3. **Where each comes from.** G: the standing approval to delete ported Python; R: the ruling; O: the census, the differential and the timings above.
4. **Do they describe the world here?** Run on this clone's real usage log, guard log and bypass records, measured 2026-11-12 (`/tmp/claude-1000/-diagram/d2dc8c63-4103-4cf9-bc83-e73a2fae792a/scratchpad/t129/diff.py`).
5. **The order.** First of the phase-3 remainder: most other slices import `usage_log`.
6. **The exits.** Green: `make static`, `make rust-test`, `make hooks-test HOOKS_ALL=1` and `make land` green. Red: what failed recorded and the task set down, a claim that it cannot be done ruled through `make arbiter-ask`.
7. **The search smell.** None.
8. **The budget.** One landing.
9. **Done, measured.** The differential's 7,854 cases with none differing, and the census.
10. **Before moving a constant.** None moved.
11. **Before fitting things into room.** Not a room question.

**Performance work?** No.

### T139 (the past features' measurement scripts that still run, `ask:449-phase3-remainder` Q4)

- **Approach**: nine of the ten scripts the ruling keeps ported whole but for two branches no input reaches (below), no door, as gate commands of the `measure` crate (`l7r-gate measure spec <feature> <name>`, `measure/spec.rs` with `spec/inventory.rs`, `spec/hamlets.rs` and `spec/runs.rs`); their 29 recorded commands rewritten to those commands and re-run; the nine `.py` deleted. The tenth, `specs/242-.../measure/note_census.py`, is in the retire class and is retired here.

   **Decisions** (`ask:449-phase3-remainder` Q4, FR-001, FR-002, FR-003):
   - The form: one gate command per past measurement, as recorded commands already name the gate script (`record agent-census`, `measure push-check-times`), run by `make figures` from the tree's top as it ran the Python; a port of a script that read its own tree reads the top (238, 239, 242, 432), one that read the working directory still reads it (261's pool, 430's run log). `spec.rs` is the one writer of the three scripts' `measurements.json` writes; one inventory parser serves 238 and 242, as 238's script loaded 242's by path.
   - The recorded commands (FR-001): 238's four, 239's two, 242's twelve, 261's nine, 430's and 432's one each, edited line by line. Re-run: 238, 239 and 242's `inventory_census` reproduce every recorded value, `make figures` listing no moved count for them; 430 reproduces its 19 runs and the `by_reason` split 11, 4, 2, 1 and 1; 432 its 7 triage findings (observed 2026-11-14, method: the rewritten commands and `l7r-gate measure figures` over the six features, `/tmp/claude-1000/-diagram/d2dc8c63-4103-4cf9-bc83-e73a2fae792a/scratchpad/t139/figures-before.log` and `figures-after.log`). 261's nine print past rounds' figures of maps the pool has since re-laid (last 2026-10-30) and do not reproduce them, the same on both sides (for example `sawada-r17-well` 173.3 recorded, 335.5 today), the round commits no object in any clone; they print and record nothing, so `make figures` compares nothing for them (observed 2026-11-14, method: each command run on both sides).
   - `note_census.py` is in the ruling's retire class: it read the old skill's per-citation HTML pages, pages feature 258 deleted (commit `3e2fe218b`), so it counts no page and all four of its recorded values move (`citation-notes` 995 to 0, `absence-notes` 260 to 0, `grounds-notes` 2 to 0, `absence-notes-never-searched` 120 to 0), and `make figures` fails on it before and after the cut (observed 2026-11-14, method: its command run and `measure figures` over 242). Its four commands are retired to `<retired: ...>` with their values kept and the script deleted, the `fr005_probe` pattern T130 followed.
   - Three defects of the shared Rust found by the differential, fixed for every crate: `serde_json`'s default float parse misread 509 of 6,000 of the maps' long floats by one place, so `float_roundtrip` is on in `rust/Cargo.toml` and the guard's manifest (0 of 6,000 with it, every crate's tests green); `math.hypot` follows CPython's own algorithm, where libm's differed in the last place on 1,760 of 300,000 pairs (0 of 300,000 after); and the guard's `pyjson::py_float` printed `inf` as `inf.0` (observed 2026-11-14, method: `/tmp/claude-1000/-diagram/d2dc8c63-4103-4cf9-bc83-e73a2fae792a/scratchpad/t139/harness/diff.py` and its float and `hypot` checks).
   - The same outputs (FR-002): HEAD's Python, frozen, against the Rust built after the deletion, each case set up identically, exit, stdout, stderr and every file written compared: 574 cases, none differing, 116 failing on both sides, over the real reports, pool, run logs and claims history and scratch trees for every branch and broken input (observed 2026-11-14, method: `/tmp/claude-1000/-diagram/d2dc8c63-4103-4cf9-bc83-e73a2fae792a/scratchpad/t139/harness/diff.py`, `diff-final.log`). Normalizations: a failing run's stderr, which in these nine is only argparse's own text or a traceback, both unbound by `ask:449-usage-text`: none of the nine writes stderr by hand, no `sys.exit("...")`, `print(..., file=sys.stderr)`, `sys.stderr.write`, `parser.error(...)` or `raise SystemExit("...")` in any (observed 2026-11-14, method: `git show HEAD:<path> | grep -cE` of those five forms over each of the nine, 0 in every one); the old `python3 ...` command in a written `measurements.json` swapped for the new on both sides, bytecode off. Two Python branches no input reaches are not carried, each commented: the census's tier-share sum, which cannot fail once no tier is stray, and triage's unpacking error, git printing no empty line. `fixtures-and-board` takes its arguments and ignores them, as the Python did.
   - Timing: `triage-price` 49.3 s in Python against 10.4 s in Rust, one streaming `git cat-file --batch` (observed 2026-11-14, method: `/tmp/claude-1000/-diagram/d2dc8c63-4103-4cf9-bc83-e73a2fae792a/scratchpad/t139/harness/diff.py`). Every other script 0.1 to 1.8 s, a little faster than its Python (observed 2026-11-14, method: the same harness). `make figures` over the six features 89 s before and 12 s after (observed 2026-11-14, method: `/tmp/claude-1000/-diagram/d2dc8c63-4103-4cf9-bc83-e73a2fae792a/scratchpad/t139/figures-before.log` and `figures-after.log`).
   - The census: no Makefile recipe, shell script or other code ran the ten (observed 2026-11-14, method: `git grep` of each name over the Makefile, `*.mk`, `*.sh`, `*.py`, `*.rs` and `.claude/`). The checks: `make static` clean on 21 crates (`measure` at 100% line coverage), `make rust-test` green (`measure` 148 tests, the guard 557), `make hooks-test HOOKS_ALL=1` green on 54 suites, the pointer check clean (observed 2026-11-14, method: those commands).

### T137 (the page sessions' tools no task held, `ask:449-phase3-remainder`)

- **Approach**: `scripts/pages/page_session_runner.py`, `brief_load.py`, `escape_log.py`, `coord.py` and `research_claims.py` ported whole, no door, into a new gate crate `pages` (`l7r-gate page-session`, `coord`, `research-claims`, `brief-load`, `escape take`), every caller repointed and the five deleted in the same cut, with `specs/274-leaner-research-sessions/measure/probe.sh`, which nothing runs.

   **Decisions** (`ask:449-phase3-remainder`, `ask:449-usage-text`, FR-001, FR-002, FR-003):
   - Its own crate, on `core`, `reviews` and the guard: the runner's ledger rows (`ledger-owed`) and `make append`'s lint and cost cells are called in process from `reviews`, with the brief count, the `WRITE_CAP_OK` escape and the sweep's feature states (where it ran `speckit-todo --each-state`); no crate below the binary has those dependencies, and an edit here rebuilds nothing else. The guard log's file naming and rename move into one helper, `shared::log::place`, which the guards' own writer also uses (FR-003).
   - The callers: the Makefile's `lines`, `append`, `research-claim` and `research-claims` run the gate commands, `LINE`, `AGENT`, `KEY` and `WHY` still read from the environment. `scripts/pages/page-session.sh` execs `l7r-gate.sh page-session`; the runner restarts its own binary as `l7r-gate page-session --work <root> <name> <extra> <queue> <runlog>` under `setsid`, its streams on `/dev/null`. `scripts/record/reserve-prefix.py`, which stays Python, runs `l7r-gate.sh escape take --token KEY_CAP_OK ...` once, only where the token is set, exit 0 taken, 1 not set, 3 the refusal it raises as the old `NoReason` (exit 2 being usage errors); where the gate cannot start it refuses without the "blocked" guard-log entry the in-process call wrote, a case nothing reaches at the cut. `brief_load` is called in process by the runner, its only importer.
   - The stall watchdog (`stall_watchdog_hooks/pass.rs`) recognizes a page-session queue by the runner's exact new argv, not loosely: its unit test rejects the old Python form and a `bash -c` naming the log, and `tests/hooks/test-stall-watchdog-hooks.sh` starts the real binary held on a sleeping step and checks the old form is no longer exempt; a Python queue still running across the cut loses its retry-wait exemption until it ends. `tests/hooks/test-no-poll-hooks.sh` reads the runner's `WAIT` constant in `runner.rs`, its `{run_log}` token unchanged.
   - `make lines` turns Python's `\Z` into the Rust regex's `\z` (the differential found `KEY='\Z'` matching every line in Python and refused in Rust). The claims sheet's lock is `flock -x` on `<sheet>.lock`, blocking as the Python's `fcntl.flock` did, so a session on the old Python and one on the Rust wait for each other. Kept as command forms with no caller (T119's rule): `brief-load`, `research-claims sweep`, `speckit-todo --each-state`.
   - The same outputs (FR-002): HEAD's Python (from `git archive HEAD`) against the Rust, each case set up identically at one path, exit, stdout, stderr and every file's bytes and mode compared: 1,727 cases, 1 differing, `research-claims -h` printing help and exiting 0 in Python and exiting 2 in Rust (`ask:449-usage-text`) (observed 2026-11-14, method: `/tmp/claude-1000/-diagram/d2dc8c63-4103-4cf9-bc83-e73a2fae792a/scratchpad/t137/diff.py`, `run-final.log` and `results-long.json`). By group: brief-load 1,247 (all 1,217 real briefs), coord 229 (copies of real handoffs, checks reports and the claims sheet), claims 90, the escape 101, the key cap 8, the four recipes through each side's Makefile 19, `make page-session` and the runner's argument errors 30, and three long cases (a retry at 60 s, the agents-returned stop at 5 min, the stall at 15 min) (observed 2026-11-14, method: the same harness). Both sides fail on every broken input: a count raising at launch, a late step and a continuation, an over-cap brief, a step that cannot run, output not UTF-8, a missing claude, a lock problem, bad `--work` JSON, a run log with no directory. The agent step was stubbed: `stub_claude.py` first on a `PATH` without `~/.local/bin`, the harness checking no other `claude` is reachable, each call logged and answered from a plan (succeed, fail with a past reset, write a continuation, hang), no real session or agent started. Normalizations: stderr from `Traceback` on, argparse's exit 2 with a `usage:` opening, the words after "KEY is not a regular expression - ", session ids and run-log names numbered in the order met, the guard-log entries' file name, `utc` and `command`, a goals line's `utc`, the stub's own environment keys, the case path in the long cases. Divergences no case reaches: non-ASCII digits in a brief number or reset time, `isdigit` read as `is_numeric`, `re` syntax beyond `\Z`, an environment value not UTF-8, a `moved-303.json` that is not an object, a command with no prompt after `-p`, ties in the claims' times read in directory order.
   - Timing: 56.1 s of process time in Python against 24.1 s in Rust over the cases, brief-load 37.8 s against 14.2 s (observed 2026-11-14, method: `/tmp/claude-1000/-diagram/d2dc8c63-4103-4cf9-bc83-e73a2fae792a/scratchpad/t137/diff.py`).
   - The census at the cut: provenance comments and `dev/phase-1-close.md`'s history; no `specs/*/measurements*.json` command runs or names any of the files; no other guard identifies a process by the runner's argv (observed 2026-11-14, method: `git grep` of each name over the Makefile, `*.mk`, `*.sh`, `*.py`, `*.rs`, `.claude/`, `tests/`, `docs`, `dev`, `scripts/container/` and every measurements file, in command, import and `-m` forms). The checks: `make static` clean on 23 crates, `make rust-test` green (`pages` 42 tests, the guard 558), `make hooks-test HOOKS_ALL=1` green on 54 suites (the stall-watchdog suite 29 passed), `check tool-signals`, `check rust-tooling`, ruff and the pointer check clean (observed 2026-11-14, method: those commands).

### T137 Approach (checklist part A)

1. **The goal, in the world.** A page session's runner, its coordination files, its claims and its escapes are Rust.
2. **The constraints.** FR-001, FR-002 and FR-003, `ask:449-phase3-remainder`, the page-session rules.

5. **The order.** After T135.
6. **The exits.** Green: `make static`, `make rust-test`, `make hooks-test HOOKS_ALL=1` and `make land` green. Red: what failed recorded and the task set down, a claim that it cannot be done ruled through `make arbiter-ask`.
7. **The search smell.** None.
8. **The budget.** One landing.
9. **Done, measured.** The differential's 1,727 cases with one ruled difference, and the census.

### T142 (ticked tasks archived out of tasks.md, the GM 2026-11-15)

- **Approach**: a ticked task's block moves from a feature's `tasks.md` into `tasks-done.md`, as its plan section already moves to `plan-done.md`, and every reader that needs ticked tasks reads both through one implementation in the guard's `shared::speckit::tasks`; feature 449's 131 ticked tasks archived in the cut.

   **Decisions** (the GM's words in `request.md`, 2026-11-15: "please do that, because I imagine that will make our long-running featuers with tons of tasks much more token efficient"; FR-002, FR-003):
   - What moves: every ticked task with an id (`- [x] Tnn`) and its indented lines, unless one of them holds an open box (such a task still holds a landing). What stays: the GM-review box (no id; `make gm-reviewed`, `ensure_box` and the done-but-GM-review-pending state read it there), the headings, `## Occasions` and the prose. No recent ticked tasks are kept: no reader needs them, and keeping a few would be a number with no reason. `tasks-done.md` holds one header line and the blocks byte for byte in id order; `tasks.md` gains one pointer line under its title and no marker where a block stood, since a column-0 marker below a task would be eaten by its next tick.
   - When: every tick archives every ticked task of its feature, not only the one it ticked, whether or not a plan section moves: the tick calls `tasks::archive(dir)`, which moves every ticked block with no open box in it (observed 2026-11-16, method: `task/src/tick.rs`'s archive call and `shared::speckit::tasks::movable`, read), so each open feature's backlog clears at its own next tick and no closed feature needs migrating. A failed move leaves the task ticked and says why. `make plan-archive F=` moves ticked tasks with plan sections; `l7r-gate.sh tick --archive <F>` moves the tasks alone, which archived 449 in the cut. The `tick-archive` usage line is recorded on every tick now, so tool-yield counts shift.
   - One implementation (FR-003): the guard's `shared::speckit::tasks` (the guard cannot build on the gate), giving the combined text, the archived blocks and the move. The readers that need ticked tasks read both: the spec-kit state (`make speckit-todo`, `BY=affects`, the closing check's push form, the glyph hour, CI), the feature-approval guard's `at_rev` (else an archived feature would read reopened and its push be refused), the plan archive and the push's plan check, the next free id (`task-add`'s `next_id` and the claims carry's `new_box`, which read `tasks.md` alone and would have handed out an archived id), the tick's and the land's "already ticked" (lowercase `[x]`, the tick's own rule), the spec lint's duplicate ids and stale citations, the research-boxes test, and the feature report's task count, tick times and `where-time`. Left reading `tasks.md` alone, each because it reads only open tasks or a file still written at every tick: the holding box, CI's feature list, set-down and its guard, the phase-source guard, the active task, the approach checks, the step-back bundle, the land's cheap pass, gm-review's box, the round counters' epochs and the shell gates; no Python reads `tasks.md` (observed 2026-11-15, method: `git grep -n "tasks.md"` over `rust/`, `scripts/`, the Makefile, `.claude/`, `.specify/`, `tests/` and `docs/`, each hit read).
   - Two defects fixed: the tick ended a task's block only at `## `, so a task above a `###` heading swallowed it and wrote its verify line below it, which had misplaced 449's T001, T005 and T070 (moved back before the archive; closed features 383 and 417 keep theirs as history), now ended at any heading with a test; and a refused land batch now also removes a `tasks-done.md` or `plan-done.md` its tick created, which `git checkout` leaves untracked.
   - The same answers (FR-002): every feature archived in a copy of the tree (307 of 319 with a `tasks.md` had tasks to move) and each reader run before and after: 1,001 outputs, none differing - the spec-kit state of 367 features with the report and its `--by-affects` view, the next id of 319, the closing reasons of 367, 4,716 tick checks over 309, the spec lint and the plan push check over every feature; the feature reports of 449, 385, 405, 444, 330, 243, 188 and 133 the same but their build-time line (observed 2026-11-15, method: `/tmp/claude-1000/-diagram/d2dc8c63-4103-4cf9-bc83-e73a2fae792a/scratchpad/t142/diff.sh`, `out-before/` and `out-after/`). Its first run found eight features whose old `- [X]` tasks changed message, so the archived lookup reads lowercase `[x]` alone, re-run to none differing.
   - End to end through make on a copy with a local bare origin: `make plan-archive F=449` moved 131 tasks; `make task-add` gave the next id and `make task-start` set it; `make tick` moved it to `tasks-done.md` and its plan sections to `plan-done.md`, and `make feature-report` found its tick; `make land` pushed one tick commit carrying the four files (observed 2026-11-15, method: `/tmp/claude-1000/-diagram/d2dc8c63-4103-4cf9-bc83-e73a2fae792a/scratchpad/t142/e2e-land2.log` and the `e2e*` trees).
   - 449 in this clone: `tasks.md` from 63,691 bytes and 463 lines to 6,040 bytes and 54 lines, six open tasks and the GM box kept, no line lost against HEAD, its state still "in progress" (observed 2026-11-15, method: `wc` before and after, and `l7r-gate.sh speckit-todo --each-state specs/449-rust-codebase`).
   - The checks: `make static` clean, `make rust-test` green on 23 crates, `make hooks-test HOOKS_ALL=1` green on 54 suites, new Rust at 100% line coverage, the pointer check clean (observed 2026-11-15, method: those commands).

### T142 Approach (checklist part A)

1. **The goal, in the world.** A long feature's `tasks.md` holds its open work, its finished tasks in `tasks-done.md`.
2. **The constraints.** FR-002 and FR-003; the GM's words.
3. **Where each comes from.** G: the GM's request of 2026-11-15; O: the differential, the make runs and 449's sizes above.
4. **Do they describe the world here?** Every feature of this clone archived in a copy and read before and after, measured 2026-11-15 (`/tmp/claude-1000/-diagram/d2dc8c63-4103-4cf9-bc83-e73a2fae792a/scratchpad/t142/diff.sh`).

### T144 (phase 4's S1, the research record's core, `ask:449-phase4-slices`)

- **Approach**: `l7r/diagram/interactive/record/`'s seventeen modules with `interactive/sources.py` and `content.py` ported as a library, the new gate crate `research` (on `core` and the guard, below `owed`, `bundle` and `record`), with no production caller: the Python stays the implementation for every Python importer until S5, S11 or S12 wires the Rust in, and is not deleted here, as the ruling's Q1 has it.

   **Decisions** (`ask:449-phase4-slices` Q1, `ask:449-T81-slices`, `ask:449-T066-json-message`, FR-001c, FR-002, FR-003):
   - One implementation (FR-003): the crate reuses what the Rust has - `units`' originals patterns and stored table, the guard's `py_text`, `pyjson`, `html_text::unescape` and `sha256`, `core`'s `read_text` - and moves into one copy what was held twice: cited-URL cleaning and the archive's URL id (`shared::cited_url`, the guard's two copies), the blocked-domain list (`shared::blocked`), `html.escape` (two private copies) and the URL's trailing-punctuation trim. Kept apart on purpose: `units::restored`, which writes "" for a missing original where `originals::restore` refuses (they port different Python), and the raw readers of `research_pointers`, `fragment_move`, `translation`, `partial_citations` and `question_size`, which refuse less than these loaders, so pointing them here would change a check's verdict on malformed input. Eleven functions nothing calls are not ported and go with their files (observed 2026-11-16, method: `git grep` of each name).
   - The two guards that read an archive's id compute it as their Python did: `archive_first_hooks` decoded six entities and `blocked_fetch_hooks` none, where the Python they replaced (`hm_fetch.archived`) decoded every entity; both now call the shared `url_id`, every suite verdict unmoved (observed 2026-11-16, method: `make hooks-test`, the blocked-fetch and archive-first suites green), a URL holding any other entity now finding its archive row as it did under the Python.
   - No process cache: the Python's per-file memo, its `@cache` readers and `clear_caches` are left to each caller's own measurement (`ask:449-T81-slices`); `sources::Reader` holds a loaded record and its cross-link and confusables tables for its lifetime. The API S2 to S5 inherit: `sources::Reader` for the cached free functions, notes as ordered pairs, sections as owned trees matched by id where the Python matched by identity.
   - `make static`'s dead check counts a `pub fn` name over every `.rs` under `rust/gate/`, tests included, so a library its own tests call passes it; no caller was added for the check (observed 2026-11-16, method: `rust dead` read and run).
   - The same outputs (FR-002, the ruling's Q1): a shim around every public function and method of the nineteen modules recorded their inputs and outputs over the Python's real runs - the record build (4,316 pages), the source-tags contract check, `check-entry-headings`, `open_questions`, `footnote_census` - and a sweep of every page, notes file, registry entry, cited and attempted URL, select term, the catalog and the numbering, with about 75 broken copies of the record for the error paths, and the six pool maps' reach into S1 (`research_questions` and `content` over every class's and kind's entry and every asset); replayed against the Rust: 378,360 calls over 118 functions, none differing, where the Python raised the Rust returning the same kind and message, `split_originals` writing 163 files byte for byte on a copied tree (observed 2026-11-16, method: `/tmp/claude-1000/-diagram/d2dc8c63-4103-4cf9-bc83-e73a2fae792a/scratchpad/t144/shim.py`, `driver.py`, `replay/src/main.rs`, `replay.out`). Normalizations: byte offsets converted to the Python's character offsets (the refusal still printing the character offset), a library's own words in a message compared up to them (`ask:449-T066-json-message`), a `KeyError`'s quotes; 336 calls made inside a load before its record stood are covered by the load's recorded output. Divergences no real case reaches: `host` neither drops tabs nor applies NFKC as `urlsplit` does, `NaN` in JSON. The sweep found and fixed Unicode digits read as Python's `int()` reads them.
   - Which later slice deletes each file: S5 `record/archive.py`, `blocked.py`, `site_notes.py`, `source_tags.py`; S11 `record/__init__.py`, `split`, `assemble`, `absence`, `contents`, `fragments`, `notes`, `originals`, `passages`, `questions`, `confusables`, `xref`, `store` and `interactive/sources.py`; S12 `interactive/content.py` (observed 2026-11-16, method: the phase-4 census, `census.tsv`). The checks: `make static` clean on 24 crates (`research` at 100% line coverage, 39 tests), `make rust-test` green (the guard 578), `make hooks-test` green on the 52 suites it ran, the pointer check clean (observed 2026-11-16, method: those commands).

### T144 Approach (checklist part A)

1. **The goal, in the world.** The research record's core has its Rust, proved on the real record, ready for the slices that wire it in.

3. **Where each comes from.** R: the ruling; O: the recorded-run differential and the census above.
4. **Do they describe the world here?** Recorded from the Python's real runs over this clone's record, measured 2026-11-16 (`/tmp/claude-1000/-diagram/d2dc8c63-4103-4cf9-bc83-e73a2fae792a/scratchpad/t144/replay.out`).
5. **The order.** First of phase 4's slices: S2 to S12 import it.
6. **The exits.** Green: `make static`, `make rust-test`, `make hooks-test` and `make land` green. Red: what failed recorded and the task set down, a claim that it cannot be done ruled through `make arbiter-ask`.
7. **The search smell.** None.
8. **The budget.** One landing.
9. **Done, measured.** 378,360 recorded calls replayed with none differing.

### T145 (phase 4's S2, T81's cut together, `ask:449-phase4-slices`)

- **Approach**: `scripts/record/quote_verbatim.py`, `source_pages.py`, `record_prepass.py`, `style_prepass.py` and `apply_edits.py` ported whole, wired and deleted; `sources.py`, `attempts.py` and `reserve-prefix.py` ported and wired for every caller, their Python cut to thin forwarders (198, 98 and 66 lines, observed 2026-11-16, method: `wc -l` of `sources.py`, `attempts.py` and `reserve-prefix.py`) that the Python still importing them calls (`archive.py` S3a, `uncited.py` and `uncited_imports.py` S3b) until S3a and S3b delete them. The ports build on S1's `research` crate (`record::*`, `sources::Reader`, `blocked`, `archive`, `fragments`) and the guard's `shared/consulted.rs` and `shared/attempts.rs`; the tools sit in `research` (`verbatim`, `pages`, `source_pages`, `prepass`, `style`), `record` (`reserve`, `sources`, `apply_edits`) and `bundle` (`record/helpers.rs`).

   **Decisions** (`ask:449-phase4-slices`, `ask:449-T80-order`, `ask:449-T81-slices`, `ask:449-T88-bundles`, `ask:449-usage-text`, `ask:449-T066-json-message`, FR-001, FR-002, FR-003):
   - The callers: the Makefile's eleven recipes (quote-verbatim, record-prepass, style-prepass, apply-edits, attempts, reserve, source-pages, `record`'s mark-filled, source-outcome, sources-consulted, sources-import) run `l7r-gate.sh record <verb>` with their arguments as they were; `tests/hooks/test-new-file-hooks.sh` runs `record reserve`; `owed/answers.rs` reads a reply in process where its inline `REPLY_OF` ran Python, and `owed/translation.rs` parses in process where its inline `READER` did; `bundle`'s `parts.rs` and `keys.rs` call the helpers in process, retiring `bundle_door.py`'s `run`, `passages` and `save_cached` verbs (its other verbs stay for their callers); the blocked-fetch guard calls `attempts::seen` in process. Doors left with no caller retire with them: `owed_door`'s `mb`, `record_door.americanize_json` (whose last caller was `apply_edits.py`) and `record_door.moved_only` (no Python caller at HEAD).
   - `translation.rs`'s `parser_key`, which hashed the two `.py` files' bytes, is the sha1 of a version string with the Rust parser's own sources (`include_str!` of `verbatim.rs`, `style.rs`, `pyre.rs`), so an edit of the parser invalidates its cache by itself; a version bump of the pinned normalization crate needs the string bumped by hand.
   - One live writer per shared file (FR-003; `ask:449-T86-door`, a name a command can carry goes by command): of the three files, the Python importers call `attempts.add` (writes `source-attempts.jsonl`; `archive.py`, `uncited.py`), `attempts.write` (the uncited filter's own lists; `uncited.py`, `uncited_imports.py`), `sources.put` (the page cache; `uncited.py`, `uncited_imports.py`) and `reserve` (`prefixes.jsonl` and the entry stub; `uncited.py`), and only read otherwise; `research_search.py` and `semantic_index.py` import none of them (observed 2026-11-16, method: each importer's calls read). So `attempts.add` forwards to `l7r-gate record attempts add` (with `--root` and `--print`), `sources.put` to a new `record sources put` (text on stdin, the page's meta back as JSON), `reserve` to `record reserve`, a failed write raising the exception the Python raised by the kind on the Rust's last line; the rest of the three files - their command lines, the ledger writers, `seed`, `import_saves`, `CachedPages`, the key cap - is removed, and `attempts.write` refuses the attempts log so `add` is its one route. Each file's one writer after: `source-attempts.jsonl` the guard's `shared::attempts`, the page cache `research::pages::put`, `prefixes.jsonl` and its stubs `record::reserve`, `sources-consulted.jsonl` the guard's `shared::consulted`, the uncited filter's lists the Python `attempts.write` (the Rust only reads them). `l7r-gate escape take`, whose one caller was the old Python reservation, retires.
   - The Python's own behavior kept where a library differs: the HTML parser is a port of CPython's, the decoders come from a table generated from CPython (`encoding_rs` differed on 7,441 byte sequences, observed 2026-11-16, method: every byte sequence of each codec decoded both ways in `/tmp/claude-1000/-diagram/d2dc8c63-4103-4cf9-bc83-e73a2fae792a/scratchpad/t145/harness/`), `unicode-normalization` is pinned to `=0.1.24` to match Python 3.14.4's NFKC, case folding from a generated table; fetching runs `curl` as an external program behind a transport seam; the Python's `ParseCache` is not carried. The three kept Python files and the Rust write the same files (`prefixes.jsonl`, `sources-consulted.jsonl`, the page cache, `source-attempts.jsonl`), so from this commit an edit to those Python files makes the same change in the Rust (`ask:449-phase4-slices`: once a slice's Rust lands, an edit of the Python under it makes the same change in the Rust in the same commit).
   - Two defects the differential found and fixed: S1's `record/source_tags.rs` read a vocabulary not UTF-8 as missing, where the Python raised `UnicodeDecodeError`; and `translation-owed` on a root that is not a directory exited 0 (so since T87), where the Python failed: it now fails as the Python did, `FileNotFoundError` or `NotADirectoryError` and exit 1, an empty directory still reporting 0 (observed 2026-11-16, method: the pre-port `translation_owed.py` at `a57ea3ad7^` against the new binary, three roots, the same).
   - The same outputs (FR-002): HEAD's Python (from a `git show HEAD:` clone) against the Rust, each case set up identically, exit, stdout, stderr and every file written compared, on copies of the real record, archive index, attempts log and registry: 1,261 cases - the prepass and style sweeps over every question (681), quote-verbatim over every question fresh and stale (367), all 3,364 archived pages through source-pages (29 batches), the fetch branches, reserve, sources, attempts, apply-edits, the Rust callers (HEAD's binary against the new) and the eleven recipes (HEAD's Makefile against the new, a refusal beside each working form) (observed 2026-11-16, method: `/tmp/claude-1000/-diagram/d2dc8c63-4103-4cf9-bc83-e73a2fae792a/scratchpad/t145/harness/``). The write paths re-run through every caller form after the forwarders: 204 cases, the five blocked-fetch guard cases (HEAD's guard running `attempts.py seen` against the in-process one) and six of the Python importers' own writes (HEAD's modules writing against this tree's forwarders, a held key, a bad kind and a blocked URL among them), none differing beyond the two below (observed 2026-11-16, method: `/tmp/claude-1000/-diagram/d2dc8c63-4103-4cf9-bc83-e73a2fae792a/scratchpad/t145/harness/``'s `importer_writes.py` and `families5.py`). Two differ: `reserve` on a `source-tags.json` that is not JSON, the parser's own words (`ask:449-T066-json-message`); and `make apply-edits` with a missing reply, the same exit and exception kind and the message text alone (`ask:449-usage-text`). Normalizations: timestamps, argparse and traceback text, a guard-log entry's file name (`<UTC to the microsecond>-<pid>.json` on both sides, varying run to run: two runs of one case on one side give two names), and `urlopen`'s text (216 cases, observed 2026-11-16, method: the harness's normalization count in `/tmp/claude-1000/-diagram/d2dc8c63-4103-4cf9-bc83-e73a2fae792a/scratchpad/t145/harness/`), which hides only that a connection failure shows `curl`'s words where Python showed its errno text (`ask:449-T066-json-message`): on a dead host the exit, stderr, the JSON report and the verdict (`UNFETCHABLE`) are the same and the fixed words around the error match, only the text inside `<urlopen error ...>` differing (observed 2026-11-16, method: question 0094 rewritten to cite a dead host and the 0323 sweep case, run raw on both sides in `/tmp/claude-1000/-diagram/d2dc8c63-4103-4cf9-bc83-e73a2fae792a/scratchpad/t145/harness/`). A guard-log entry the key cap's escape writes names its own process in its `command` field, `l7r-gate record reserve` where it named `reserve-prefix.py`, as the guard log's `command` always records the process that wrote it, so `make audit` names the Rust there (the `ask:449-T135-generator` case: a record's own text naming the tool that wrote it). The network was stubbed: a loopback server served the recorded archive pages with synthetic redirects, a loop, a PDF, binary, Shift-JIS, Latin-1 and a slow page, dead proxies set on both sides and `archive.py` stubbed, and a logging `curl` over the unit tests saw only 127.0.0.1 (observed 2026-11-16, method: the harness's stub and shim).
   - Timing, recorded and not held: quote-verbatim 178 s in Python against 132 s in Rust (observed 2026-11-16, method: `/tmp/claude-1000/-diagram/d2dc8c63-4103-4cf9-bc83-e73a2fae792a/scratchpad/t145/harness/`). The prepass and style sweeps 230 s against 337 s, the Rust regex engine backtracking where Python's `re` does not (observed 2026-11-16, method: `/tmp/claude-1000/-diagram/d2dc8c63-4103-4cf9-bc83-e73a2fae792a/scratchpad/t145/harness/`). The archive sweep 41 s against 88 s, unprofiled, `curl` started once a page the likely cause (observed 2026-11-16, method: `/tmp/claude-1000/-diagram/d2dc8c63-4103-4cf9-bc83-e73a2fae792a/scratchpad/t145/harness/`). The ledger and edit tools at or below the Python's (observed 2026-11-16, method: `/tmp/claude-1000/-diagram/d2dc8c63-4103-4cf9-bc83-e73a2fae792a/scratchpad/t145/harness/`). A quadratic tag scanner the sweeps found, 2 s on one page and 0.05 s after, was rewritten and checked against the Python on 400 random pages, none differing (observed 2026-11-16, method: `/tmp/claude-1000/-diagram/d2dc8c63-4103-4cf9-bc83-e73a2fae792a/scratchpad/t145/harness/`).
   - The census: no `specs/*/measurements*.json` command runs the eight; 375's two rows `375-a8-check-bundle` and `375-a8-check-bundle-after` name three of them as timing keys: their commands are one-shot runs of `make check-bundle`, a target that stays (its helpers now Rust in process), and a one-shot row `make figures` does not re-run, its values kept as the record of that day (observed 2026-11-16, method: `git grep` of each name, command, import and `-m` forms, at HEAD and after). ### T143 (the shell libraries' inline Python, `ask:449-phase4-slices` Q12)

- **Approach**: every inline Python site of `scripts/hooks/lib/guardlog.sh`, `scripts/hooks/lib/clone-resolve.sh` and `.specify/scripts/bash/common.sh` replaced by the Rust, no door: `guard_log` calls a new gate command `l7r-gate log guard` over the guard crate's one guard-log writer (`shared::log::write_entry`) and one session resolver (`shared::session`); `common.sh`'s four sites (six `python3` lines) go, two ported - the `feature.json` read and the presets - calling `l7r-gate speckit feature-dir` and `speckit presets` (the `author` crate); `clone-resolve.sh`, whose one caller was `guardlog.sh`, and `common.sh`'s `resolve_template_content`, which nothing calls, deleted. The shell functions keep their names and arguments, so the five `*-gate.sh`, `LOGESCAPE`, `sync-with-main.sh`, `l7r-guard.sh` and the `.specify` scripts do not change.

   **Decisions** (`ask:449-phase4-slices` Q12, `ask:449-T051-lib-route`, `ask:449-usage-text`, FR-001, FR-002, FR-003):
   - The gate binary, not the guard's through `l7r-guard.sh`: every caller but one has just run `l7r-gate.sh escape reason-ok`, so the gate binary is current; the suites' fixture trees link the real `l7r-gate.sh` where the guard binary is found under a `$HOME` they move; and `l7r-guard.sh`'s no-binary path calls `guard_log` itself, so routing through it would loop. That one hook-time caller never waits on a build: it runs under `L7R_GATE_STALE_OK=1` and a new `L7R_GATE_NO_BUILD=1` seam of `l7r-gate.sh`.
   - The no-binary entry: `l7r-guard.sh`'s no-binary path tries the gate's writer first and, where that exits nonzero because the gate has no binary either, writes its "failed-open" entry through `scripts/hooks/lib/failed-open-log.sh`, which needs neither Python nor a binary (`jq -a --indent 2`, a `printf` path where `jq` is absent), byte for byte the entry HEAD's Python wrote on that path: its fields and order, `payload.get(k) or ""`, the `SID` fallback, the session name resolved as `clone-resolve.sh` did, the file name's form, written to a temporary and renamed. It is that one path's alone, the only record that the guards did not run on a tree with nothing built; every other entry keeps the one Rust writer. `guard_log` is a wrapper that always returns 0, its work in `_guard_log_write`, whose exit only the no-binary path reads. Edges named in the file's header: a float literal `jq` reads otherwise than Python (`nan` in lower case), and without `iconv` an input not UTF-8 that also holds a real U+FFFD.
   - A payload's numbers read as Python read them: `pyjson::loads`, scoped to the guard log's reader, keeps an integer's digits past u64 and reads `NaN`, `Infinity` and floats past a double's range as Python's JSON did, held as marked strings `pyjson::dumps` writes back bare (where the Rust wrote `1.2345678901234568e+29` for Python's `123456789012345678901234567890`); not serde_json's `arbitrary_precision`, a feature of the whole build that would change every crate's numbers (`1.50` written as read where Python writes `1.5`); no other crate's output moves, every crate's tests green.
   - Toward the Python, every writer and resolver sharing them: `pyjson::ascii_string` escapes 0x7f as `ensure_ascii` does (a core test that pinned it bare was wrong against the Python), changing the bytes of `log run`, `log bypass`, `escape take` and the guard log for that one character; the guards' own entries share the shell's writer; the shared resolver (clone-sync's routing reads it too) resolves the cwd to its real path, skips dot files among the sessions, reads Python's whitespace in the kebab-case name and an empty `CLONE_SESSIONS_DIR`, `HOME` or `GUARD_LOG_DIR` as unset (`/diagram` and the clone are not symlinks, so live routing does not move). `l7r-gate` takes its arguments as bytes: `log guard` decodes them as Python's `surrogateescape` did, and any other subcommand handed one not UTF-8 exits 101 with a message where it panicked.
   - The same outputs (FR-002): HEAD's shell (its inline Python as it was) against the new, each case set up identically at one path, exit, stdout, stderr and every file written compared: 2,194 cases in two runs, none differing, with 364 spec-kit cases in a third, none differing (observed 2026-11-16, method: `/tmp/claude-1000/-diagram/d2dc8c63-4103-4cf9-bc83-e73a2fae792a/scratchpad/t143/diff.py`, `run-final2.log`, `results.json`) - the guard log 1,166 (400 real entries rebuilt as payloads against the real clones, sessions and transcripts read-only, 250 recorded hook inputs, 253 resolver branches on scratch layouts, 125 payload shapes with integers past u64 and `NaN`, 22 argument forms, 7 log-directory cases, and every sourcer's real call: 18 gate escapes and refusals, 6 `LOGESCAPE`, 5 `sync-with-main` lines, 80 no-binary runs on real payloads), the no-binary entry with the gate binary absent too 1,028 (400 real payloads, 250 fixture inputs, 125 shapes, 253 resolver cases), and, in the third run (`results-speckit.json`), the spec-kit functions 364 (every `feature.json` form and preset registry, with and without `jq`, through each function and `check-prerequisites.sh`, `setup-plan.sh` and `setup-tasks.sh`). Normalizations: an entry's `utc` and file name (nanoseconds then, microseconds now, as T137), a bypass record's name and `utc`. End to end: gate escapes in the scratch tree, `create-new-feature.sh` on a scratch mirror and clone the same both sides, `check-prerequisites.sh --json` the same in the real clone, `test-sync-with-main.sh` green, and `test-l7r-guard.sh`'s new case comparing the fallback's entry with HEAD's Python's bytes (observed 2026-11-16, method: `/tmp/claude-1000/-diagram/d2dc8c63-4103-4cf9-bc83-e73a2fae792a/scratchpad/t143/e2e-claim.sh` and those runs).

### T159 (the plan review's commonest unreviewable return, a count no label reaches; the GM 2026-11-16, request.md)

- **Approach**: `make decide`'s lint (`rust/gate/crates/plan/src/plan/lint.rs`, which `make plan-delta` asks too) refuses a sentence stating a count - a number before a noun this project's plans count by measuring (lines, cases, files, pages, calls, crates, suites, tests, rows, keys, findings, differences, runs, commits, bytes and their kin) - with no label in that sentence, as it already refuses a figure with a physical unit; its message names the labels and says to re-read the count from the run's own record after the last edit.

   **Decisions** (the GM's words in request.md, 2026-11-16; FR-001's tooling, feature 385 T86 and feature 430 D5, whose check it extends):
   - Why: of four port agents' time, the checks took 5-14% and the differentials 2-30%, the rest the model's own work (observed 2026-11-16, method: each tool call's wait and each background wait in the agents' transcripts, `/tmp/claude-1000/-diagram/c6fd72d1-ab6c-4736-b723-0697a1f5ca51/scratchpad/agent_time.py`); the avoidable cost was the review's round trips, and T145's plan took five dispatches, three of them returned for a figure - two unlabeled, then one count misreported (observed 2026-11-16, method: this session's dispatches and their replies). Each such return costs a dispatch, a rewrite and a fresh `make decide`.
   - The nouns are counts a plan measures; the plan's own parts ("14 decisions", "two tasks", "11 recipes") name and do not measure, so they stay out; a rule's threshold ("no file over 1,000 lines", "at most 10 keys") states a limit and is exempt; a date, a task or requirement id and a code span are not figures, as the unit check already reads them.
   - A count is split by sentence only, where the unit check splits at ";" too: over the sixteen reviewed sections of 449 from T121 to T145, the ";" split flagged 11 counts their reviews had passed and the sentence split 3, each a count no label reached - "110 `.py` files" (T134), "124 cases" (T134), "336 calls" (T144) (observed 2026-11-16, method: `/tmp/claude-1000/-diagram/c6fd72d1-ab6c-4736-b723-0697a1f5ca51/scratchpad/figcheck/proto2.py`, the rule mirrored in Python, over `plan-done.md`). The tick's own "**Done, measured.**" lines, written after the review, were left out of that count.
   - It catches the case that filed it: T145's `(183, 98 and 57 lines)` is refused and its labeled form passes, pinned by the lint's tests.
   - Kept with it: every port task's brief from T147 on asks for each figure re-measured after the agent's last edit, with its method. The GM's second proposal - the differentials rerunning only what a fix touched - is enforced by tooling, as the GM's 2026-11-11 words ask ("our tooling must enforce this"), so it is its own task, T161: one shared runner in the repository keying each case by the inputs and code it runs, rerunning after a fix only the cases whose key moved, the port briefs using it. The third proposal, compile and test speed, is T160, ordered last as the GM was shown it, opening with a measurement of where compile and test time goes.
   - The checks: the plan crate's tests green, its line coverage complete (observed 2026-11-16, method: `make rust-test CRATE=rust/gate/crates/plan` and `l7r-gate.sh rust uncovered --crate rust/gate/crates/plan`).

### T159 Approach (checklist part A)

1. **The goal, in the world.** A plan section reaches its review with every count labeled, so no round is spent on one.
2. **The constraints.** The GM's words (request.md, 2026-11-16); feature 430 D5's rule that a plan review is never dispatched on what a script can see.
3. **Where each comes from.** G: the GM's approval; O: the transcript split and the sixteen-section measurement above.
4. **Do they describe the world here?** Measured on this feature's own reviewed sections, measured 2026-11-16 (`/tmp/claude-1000/-diagram/c6fd72d1-ab6c-4736-b723-0697a1f5ca51/scratchpad/figcheck/proto2.py`).
5. **The order.** After T146; before T147, whose plan it checks first.
6. **The exits.** Green: the plan crate's tests and coverage, and `make land` green. Red: what failed recorded and the task set down, a claim that it cannot be done ruled through `make arbiter-ask`.
7. **The search smell.** None.
8. **The budget.** One landing.
9. **Done, measured.** The lint's tests, and T147's plan reaching its review with no figure returned.
10. **Before moving a constant.** None moved.
11. **Before fitting things into room.** Not a room question.

**Performance work?** No - it saves review rounds, not running time.

It follows fastembed's tokenizer setup, batches of 8, Level3 graph optimization, half the online cores (the docstring's memory reason), the CLS row and numpy's pairwise float32 norm; batching matters, a vector alone and in a batch differing (observed 2026-11-16, method: one passage embedded alone and in a batch of 8 on both sides). Its own binary like the browser (`ask:449-T146-browser`'s pattern): no gate or guard crate depends on it (`cargo tree`), the make-only guard refuses `l7r-embed` bare (FR-005) and the claims walk prunes `embed`, each with a test.

### T163 (a defect T148 found in the record check, fixed in its own commit as constitution XIV asks)

- **Approach**: the record check (`make record CHECK=1`, which the push's preflight and its record row run) keeps a passing result keyed on its inputs and the program, and its refusals read today's date: an archive row whose upload is pending answers for its URL for seven days. A pass kept on one day was replayed on a later one, past a row's window, letting through a record the check now refuses. The key of the record's check now holds today's UTC date (`rust/gate/crates/research/src/tools/memo.rs`); the glossary's, which reads no date, is unchanged.

   **Decisions** (constitution XIV, a defect fixed where it is found; FR-002, which held T148's port to the Python's key so that this change is its own):
   - Where it came from: T148's port first added the date inside the port, and its plan review held that FR-002's fix exception covers a check that refuses correct work, not one made to refuse more, so the port kept the Python's key and this task fixes the check on its own; `escalation-check` cut the question of asking first, constitution XIV deciding it (observed 2026-11-16, method: T148's plan review and the escalation check's reply).
   - What it costs: the kept pass is rerun once a day, the check fresh taking 2.2 s where a kept pass takes 0.06 s (observed 2026-11-16, method: `/usr/bin/time` of the record check fresh and kept, T148).

### T165 (the claims tools over Rust units before the engine ports; the GM 2026-11-17, request.md)

- **Approach**: the claims crate (`rust/gate/crates/claims/`) gains the two pieces that worked on Python units alone: the stale-figure check over a Rust `const` or `static` carrying `Research:` (`stale.rs`) and the counter-only clear over Rust counter statements (`counters.rs`); a Rust unit's bundle carries the context a Python unit's does (`context.rs`); and three gaps the end-to-end run found are fixed - the merge-base read, the push's claims gate and `tunables --inline` reading `rust/`.

   **Decisions** (the GM's words, request.md 2026-11-17; `ask:449-phase4-slices` Q10; FR-002 for the Python units' outputs; constitution XIV):
   - Stale figures on Rust: a `const` or `static` (one in an `impl` too) whose own doc holds `Research:` and whose value or doc changed since the merge base has its base value's number literals read as Python writes them (`43_560.0` as `43560`, `0.35f64` as `0.35`), 0 and 1 left out as the Python leaves them, and the drawing pages still stating one named in `claims_stale.py`'s own line; the Python path is unchanged and still asked only when a `.py` under `l7r/` changed. A real change, `BEND_WIDTHS` 2.5 to 3.0, names the page stating 2.5, where HEAD names none (observed 2026-11-17, method: a scratch clone with the change, `/tmp/claude-1000/-diagram/c6fd72d1-ab6c-4736-b723-0697a1f5ca51/scratchpad/t165/demo-c.log`).
   - Counter-only clear on Rust: a counter statement is a `#[cfg(feature = "counters")]` block or statement (a gated `if` or `for` refused) or a `tally`, `merge`, aliased `tally` or `counts.add` call whose key is the counters' `kind@function` form and whose value uses only numbers, places, `.len()`, integer casts, `*`, `+` and parentheses; a claim is cleared only when its recorded code is the base's and the unit is that code plus added counter statements. Of the 98 counter call sites in `rust/phases`, 79 are of that form, the other 19 owing a check as before (observed 2026-11-17, method: the form run over every call site). A real counter gained in `sink::sink` clears its claim, where HEAD owes a code triage (observed 2026-11-17, method: `/tmp/claude-1000/-diagram/c6fd72d1-ab6c-4736-b723-0697a1f5ca51/scratchpad/t165/demo-c2.log`).
   - The context a Rust unit's bundle carries follows the Python rules - its own file's callees up to six, every constant it reads, two call levels for a distance claim, the CANNOT-TELL chase - names resolved through the file's items or its `use` lines; bundles grew from a median of 11.6 to 15.4 KB (observed 2026-11-17, method: every claimed Rust unit's bundle built before and after).
   - Gaps fixed (constitution XIV): the merge-base read listed no `rust/` path, so a finding on unchanged Rust code read as introduced; the push's claims gate judged no `rust/` path, so a delta touching only `rust/phases` pushed with its owed claims unchecked, and now runs the gate, 0.65 s warm (observed 2026-11-17, method: `/tmp/claude-1000/-diagram/c6fd72d1-ab6c-4736-b723-0697a1f5ca51/scratchpad/t165/demo-d.log`, HEAD's binary against the new); `tunables --inline` read `rust/phases` alone and now reads every crate the claims walk reads.
   - Where the engine ports go: the claims walk reads every crate under `rust/` but `target`, `parked`, `guard`, `gate`, `browser` and `embed`, a new crate walked with nothing declared (a test holds it), so an engine slice's Rust lands in its own crate beside `rust/phases`, never under `rust/gate/`.
   - Left for T166, measured: a claim does not carry from a deleted `.py` unit onto its Rust port, carry matching by code fingerprint, which a `.py` and a `.rs` unit never share (367 `.py` claims), and a Rust unit's fingerprint does not hold the constants it reads, as a Python unit's does (111 of 398 claimed Rust functions read one); both are fixed before any engine slice (observed 2026-11-17, method: a scratch port of two claimed constants to a new crate, and the units' reads counted).

VERIFY=1`, `/tmp/claude-1000/-diagram/c6fd72d1-ab6c-4736-b723-0697a1f5ca51/scratchpad/t165/diffrun/same-cases.diff-run/reports/diff-run-verify-20261117T070029Z.json`)); the Rust cases differ only in the new lines this task adds, each named (measured 2026-11-17 (`make diff-run ... ### T166 (the claims tooling's two gaps T165 measured, closed before any engine slice; the GM 2026-11-17, request.md)

- **Approach**: (1) a claim carries from a deleted `.py` unit onto its Rust port through a committed port map, `dev/claims-ports.json`, which `claims rekey` (run by `make land`) reads; the push's claims gate refuses a claimed `.py` unit deleted with no move and no map entry, naming the line to add (`rust/gate/crates/claims/src/claims/ports.rs`); (2) a Rust unit's fingerprint holds the values of the crate constants it reads, as a Python unit's does, and a check records those values on its row (`reads.rs`), the landed rows migrated without re-checking anything (`make claims-refingerprint`).

   **Decisions** (`ask:449-phase4-slices` Q10, `ask:449-T148-claims`; the GM's words, request.md 2026-11-17; FR-002 for the Python units' outputs; FR-008):
   - The port map is one shared file, each entry naming the slice that wrote it (`by`), because the claims tools read a fixed path at every tree, the merge base's included; a later feature's port uses the same map.
   - The carry (Q10's "re-keyed there with claims carry"): a row of a mapped unit that is gone is re-keyed onto the same label of its Rust unit when that unit carries the claim's own text (the row's, or the merge base's Python unit's for an older row that stored none), keeps its verdict, note and pages with its old key under `ported`, and is owed `ported` - a full check, never a triage or counter clear - so the landing's claims round checks the Rust code (Q10's "That cut's landing runs the claims check"); the deferred list is re-keyed with it; a no-research claim ported into a pruned tooling crate is dropped (`ask:449-T148-claims`) and one citing research is refused as a new ask.
   - Demonstrated on a scratch clone: `DRAFT_MARGIN_FT`, `CAPTION_ROOM` and `_wall_clearance_ft` ported from `compound.py` to a new `rust/mode_a` and the Python deleted; before the map the gate refused all three as unported, with it `rekey` carried the three rows and the gate owed them as ported, and a real `impl-drift` round on the claims bundle found all three IN-STEP on the Rust code and one UNCLAIMED figure the scratch port wrote out as literals, after which none was owed and the gate passed (observed 2026-11-17, method: `/tmp/claude-1000/-diagram/c6fd72d1-ab6c-4736-b723-0697a1f5ca51/scratchpad/t166/demo-port.log` and `demo-round-*`).
   - The fingerprint: a unit's code key adds `NAME=<value>` for each constant of its crate it reads, resolved as T165's context resolves names, keyed by name so a moved constant owes nothing; a check records the read values on its row, so a changed value owes the reader - which also closes the relabel shortcut that let a reader whose own text is unchanged pass. Rows whose recorded fingerprint equals the old scheme's are re-recorded in the same change, one line a run in `dev/claims-refingerprint.jsonl`: 286 rows of the 112 claimed Rust units that read a constant, `make claims-owed` owing none before and none after, `make claims-report` identical to HEAD's (observed 2026-11-17, method: those commands before and after the migration). ### T160 (compile and test speed, the GM's third approved proposal, request.md 2026-11-16; measured first)

- **Approach**: measured first where a port task's compile and test time goes, then took the targets with a measured saving: the checks runner (`rust/gate/crates/rustc/`) runs the owed crates' already-built test binaries directly, five at once, caches each file's code views by path and blob id, and has `dead` count the crate family's words once a run; the slowest crates' tests brought down (archive, diffrun, browser, bundle, task, tree), the flaky tests the side-by-side run exposed made deterministic, two leaks into the shared `/tmp` closed, and an archive defect fixed. The rest of FR-008's debt is T167.

   **Decisions** (the GM's words, request.md 2026-11-16; FR-008, FR-010, FR-011, FR-013; docs/performance-checklist.md; constitution XIV):
   - Where the time went: on an unchanged tree `make rust-test` took 1.2 s and `make static` 4.6 s, most of it rereading and hashing every `.rs` file for the keys (observed 2026-11-17, method: `/tmp/claude-1000/-diagram/c6fd72d1-ab6c-4736-b723-0697a1f5ca51/scratchpad/t160/notes.md`); after a one-line edit of `owed` `make rust-test` took 23.4 s, about 10 s of it the twelve moved crates' tests run one after another through `cargo test`, and `make static` 36.9 s, 5.8 s of it `dead` recounting the family for each of 27 crates (observed 2026-11-17, method: `/tmp/claude-1000/-diagram/c6fd72d1-ab6c-4736-b723-0697a1f5ca51/scratchpad/t160/notes.md`); the worst single crates' tests were archive's 6.1 s and diffrun's 4.4 s (observed 2026-11-17, method: each scenario timed, `/tmp/claude-1000/-diagram/c6fd72d1-ab6c-4736-b723-0697a1f5ca51/scratchpad/t160/notes.md`).
   - The runner, which removes work rather than moving it: the test binaries the key's build already names run directly, five at a time, in place of serial `cargo test` (a crate whose binaries the build does not name keeps `cargo test`); a file's code views are kept by path and blob id in `.git/rust-checks/code-views`, keyed to the `l7r-rust` binary, and not computed at all for `format` and `dead`; `dead` counts the family once. After: an unchanged tree's `make static` 1.9 s and `make rust-test` 0.55 s (observed 2026-11-17, method: `/tmp/claude-1000/-diagram/c6fd72d1-ab6c-4736-b723-0697a1f5ca51/scratchpad/t160/notes.md`); `dead` after a gate edit 0.7 s (observed 2026-11-17, method: `/tmp/claude-1000/-diagram/c6fd72d1-ab6c-4736-b723-0697a1f5ca51/scratchpad/t160/notes.md`); the `owed` edit's `make rust-test` 20.1 s and `make static` 27.3 s (observed 2026-11-17, method: the same scenarios at similar load, `/tmp/claude-1000/-diagram/c6fd72d1-ab6c-4736-b723-0697a1f5ca51/scratchpad/t160/notes.md`). All 31 crates' tests at once took 25.0 to 26.9 s in each of 24 runs (observed 2026-11-17, method: `/tmp/claude-1000/-diagram/c6fd72d1-ab6c-4736-b723-0697a1f5ca51/scratchpad/t160/passrate5.txt`, the host's one-minute load 24 to 75 from other containers).
   - The slowest tests (FR-008), every assertion kept: archive's crate 6.06 to 0.37 s (its per-host gap a field, its client and inbox tests split), diffrun's 4.4 to 0.6 s (a 50 ms second in the test build alone), browser's 2.0 to 0.73 s (now bounded by its real-Chromium test), bundle's 1.32 to 0.45 s, task's glob tests 0.48 to 0.05 s, tree's needs test 0.40 to 0.08 s (observed 2026-11-17, method: `/tmp/claude-1000/-diagram/c6fd72d1-ab6c-4736-b723-0697a1f5ca51/scratchpad/t160/notes.md`); across the workspace 151 tests remain over the bar where 159 were, the worst 0.90 s where it was 6.05 s (observed 2026-11-17, method: each test alone, `/tmp/claude-1000/-diagram/c6fd72d1-ab6c-4736-b723-0697a1f5ca51/scratchpad/t160/ws-after.rows`). Those 151, and the ruling on the real-tree tests no tool declares its one end-to-end test, are T167's.
   - Flaky tests fixed at their source, not by narrowing the runner: land's claims wait now takes a clock (the real one by default), its test a clock that moves only when the wait sleeps; pages' stall stub removes its fake `/proc` entry when it dies, as a real one would; the trials fixture's perf report no longer stamped "now" (failing 6 of 96 runs eight at a time before, none of 96 after); fake executables written by `install`, closing the "Text file busy" race (observed 2026-11-17, method: each crate's tests eight copies at once, `/tmp/claude-1000/-diagram/c6fd72d1-ab6c-4736-b723-0697a1f5ca51/scratchpad/t160/`). Stress at eight copies: pages none of 80 failed; land one of the first 80 and none of the next 240, that one's log lost, so it is not shown to be load.
   - `/tmp` (FR-013): its 8,536 entries almost all predate T101; two leaks still live were closed - the make-only suite's fixed `/tmp/mo.out` and two tests writing into the real `/tmp/l7r-check` - and a full `make rust-test` and `make hooks-test HOOKS_ALL=1` now leave nothing new there (observed 2026-11-17, method: `/tmp` listed before and after). The old entries cost about 20 ms a temporary directory outside `make rust-test`, under 2 s across the measured scenarios (observed 2026-11-17, method: `/tmp/claude-1000/-diagram/c6fd72d1-ab6c-4736-b723-0697a1f5ca51/scratchpad/t160/notes.md`), so the sweep is not extended to them.
   - Defect fixed (constitution XIV): the archive's sync of the GM's copies committed files over GitHub's limit (`100 MB`, its own constant), after which every archive push fails, as the Python did; it now refuses them first, a test pinning it and failing with the fix taken out.
   - Dropped, measured: building every crate in one cargo call (features unify differently; the first run took 81 s and left a second artifact set, observed 2026-11-17, method: one cargo call over every crate, `/tmp/claude-1000/-diagram/c6fd72d1-ab6c-4736-b723-0697a1f5ca51/scratchpad/t160/notes.md`), and the gate's duplicated Python tests (its design, not this task's).
   - The checks: `make static` green, `make rust-test` green, `make hooks-test HOOKS_ALL=1` green on 54 suites (observed 2026-11-17, method: those commands, one after another after the last edit).

### T160 Approach (checklist part A)

1. **The goal, in the world.** A port task's checks rerun only what moved, run what they must side by side, and no test of the slowest crates waits on real time.

5. **The order.** After T166; T167 after it.
6. **The exits.** Green: `make static`, `make rust-test`, `make hooks-test HOOKS_ALL=1` and `make land` green. Red: what failed recorded and the task set down, a claim that it cannot be done ruled through `make arbiter-ask`.
7. **The search smell.** None.
8. **The budget.** One landing.
9. **Done, measured.** The before-and-after figures above and the pass loop.
10. **Before moving a constant.** None moved.
11. **Before fitting things into room.** Not a room question.

**Performance work?** Yes, of the tooling, not the generator: (1) the time went to rehashing every file, serial test runs and `dead`'s recount, measured per scenario; (2) each change removes work - a kept view, binaries run directly and side by side, one count; (3) the expected saving was the serial test time and `dead`'s 5.8 s, both measured (observed 2026-11-17, method: `/tmp/claude-1000/-diagram/c6fd72d1-ab6c-4736-b723-0697a1f5ca51/scratchpad/t160/notes.md`); (4) the work grows with the crates and files changed, no longer with the whole tree; (5) before and after under similar load, the spread over 24 runs (observed 2026-11-17, method: `/tmp/claude-1000/-diagram/c6fd72d1-ab6c-4736-b723-0697a1f5ca51/scratchpad/t160/passrate5.txt`), stated as evidence; (6) no map moved.

### T169 (the engine pilot's no-brainer process fixes; the GM 2026-11-17, request.md: pre-approved where clearly beneficial and without a downside)

- **Approach**: four fixes the pilot (T168) found, each with no downside beyond its build: the shared runner builds a world as a sparse checkout of the paths a case declares (`rust/gate/crates/diffrun/src/checkout.rs`); `make static` checks the claims form of every crate the claims walk reads (`claims coverage --rust`); the plan review's bundle carries every ruling a changed block cites (`rust/gate/crates/plan/src/plan/bundle/rulings.rs`, its `rulings.md`); and `make test-times CRATE=<dir>` times each test alone by T99's method (`rust/gate/crates/rustc/src/rustc/times.rs`).

   **Decisions** (the GM's words in request.md, 2026-11-17; FR-008; the GM's performance rule, docs/performance-checklist.md):
   - Sparse worlds, for iterating only, after the plan review: a cases file's `world.checkout` names a repository, a revision (`WORKTREE` laying the uncommitted and untracked files of its paths over HEAD) and the paths to check out, and incremental, `--only` and `--twice` runs build those sparse worlds; a `--verify` or `--all` run ALWAYS builds whole checkouts, ignoring the list, both sides keyed by the kind of world and kept apart (`.whole.json`), so a too-narrow list - both sides failing alike, which reads as agreement - can pass an incremental run but never a verify, the only report a plan may cite (T161's lint), and no sparse result stands in it. A test holds it: a list too narrow for its case passes the sparse run and differs in the verify, and the test fails with the verify's rule taken out (observed 2026-11-17, method: the rule deleted and restored). On T168's cases the incremental run took 50.0 s on sparse worlds against 267.1 s on whole ones, the first verify after it 265.6 s and a second 131.5 s (observed 2026-11-17, method: each from a fresh state, `/tmp/claude-1000/-diagram/c6fd72d1-ab6c-4736-b723-0697a1f5ca51/scratchpad/t169/demo/`), every kept result, whole and sparse, equal to a whole checkout's (observed 2026-11-17, method: the results compared). So the saving is the iterating runs', and a verify's figures stay the record.
   - The claims form at `make static`: a unit with no claim of its own and no module-level claim is refused there, before landing, with the fix in the message; the check takes 0.05 to 0.06 s (observed 2026-11-17, method: three runs on an unchanged tree and after an edit). It reads every walked crate, so it is stricter than the push's gate, which reads changed files: an unchanged file whose claim's pointer breaks is refused at `make static` too, which the tree passes today. The comment on `walked()` now says a new crate owes a claim on every unit.
   - Rulings in the bundle: for each `ask:<key>` a changed block cites, its record's date, ruling, why and what, verbatim, from the feature's own arbiter log first; a key with no record is named as such. On T168's section the bundle carried `ask:449-engine-order` and the other cited rulings, none missing (observed 2026-11-17, method: `make plan-delta` on a scratch clone).
   - The timer reports and never refuses, the GM's performance rule making time never a gate; on `rust/mode_a` it agreed with T168's hand timings (observed 2026-11-17, method: both run on the crate).
   - The checks: `make static`, `make rust-test` and `make hooks-test HOOKS_ALL=1` green (observed 2026-11-17, method: those commands, one after another after the last edit).

7. **The search smell.** None.

### T172 (T170's claims round: units of rust/mode_a ran past the statics after a raw string)

- **Approach**: the claims walk's Rust item splitter (`rust/gate/crates/claims/src/claims/units.rs`, `item_end`) reads a raw string literal (`r"..."`, `r#"..."#`, `br#"..."#`) to its own close - a quote followed by its own hashes, a backslash escaping nothing - where it read one as a plain string, so a raw pattern's first inner quote closed it and the unit ran on past the next items, which got no key. T170's impl-drift round named the units it swallowed in `parse.rs`, `labels.rs`, `shapes.rs`, `sheet.rs` and `tagged.rs`.

   **Decisions** (constitution XIV; FR-001; the GM's words, request.md 2026-11-17, no-brainer process fixes pre-approved):
   - A defect of the walk fixed where found (XIV): a unit whose span is wrong gives its claim a code hash over the wrong text and leaves the statics after it unjudged. No tradeoff: the fix only adds keys and narrows spans to what the item is; nothing it changes refuses a landing beyond the round below.
   - Proved: a test reads statics after a raw literal with inner quotes, a byte raw literal with fewer hashes inside, a raw literal ending in a backslash, a raw identifier and an unclosed raw literal; it went red with `units.rs` stashed and green with it back (observed 2026-11-17, method: `git stash push` of the file, `make rust-test CRATE=rust/gate/crates/claims`, `git stash pop`).
   - Its reach, measured: `make claims-owed` after the fix owes 32 new claims, every one in T170's files in `rust/mode_a`, and 18 claims of units the fix reshaped, owed in full (observed 2026-11-17, method: `make claims-owed`, `make claims-triage`). No other crate's unit moved, so nothing landed earlier is re-judged; the round runs here, one impl-drift bundle.

### T173 (T170's verify run spent nearly all its time building worlds, not running its cases)

- **Approach**: the shared differential runner (`rust/gate/crates/diffrun/`) runs a run's owed sides on n workers when asked - `make diff-run CASES=... JOBS=n`, the binary's `--jobs n`, default 1 - each worker in its own world (`work/<side>-<w>`, `work/<side>` when one), the main thread alone building each row and printing its line in case order, builds once before any case. Where the time went: T170's verify run took 392.6 s and its sides' own commands 11.6 s of it, the rest a whole world built and removed for each side one after another (observed 2026-11-17, method: T170's verify report's `wall_s` against the sum of its sides' `took_s`).

   **Decisions** (the GM's words, request.md 2026-11-17, no-brainer process fixes pre-approved; FR-002, FR-008):
   - Opt-in, the default unchanged: a cases file whose harness writes a fixed path outside its world would race on several workers, so JOBS is the caller's to set where the harness writes only inside `{WORLD}`, which docs/diff-run.md states. With JOBS unset a run is today's.
   - The result is the serial run's: the report, the kept results and the printed lines in case order, an error naming a worker's world rewritten to the serial path. Proved by a test running three cases whose sides finish out of start order at JOBS=1 and JOBS=4, equal but for the clock, each worker's world its own; it and the clamp test went red under four mutations - rows in completion order, one shared world, the clamp removed, the error path not rewritten (observed 2026-11-17, method: each mutation in a scratch copy of `runner.rs` restored by `cp`, `make rust-test CRATE=rust/gate/crates/diffrun`).
   - Measured on T170's 105 cases, VERIFY=1, whole worlds, every side rerun from a fresh state directory: JOBS=1 375.8 s, JOBS=2 220.5 s, JOBS=4 151.5 s, JOBS=6 162.2 s, JOBS=8 181.6 s, every report 105 cases none differing and equal to the serial one but for the clock (observed 2026-11-17, method: `make diff-run CASES=/tmp/claude-1000/-diagram/c6fd72d1-ab6c-4736-b723-0697a1f5ca51/scratchpad/t173/m<J>/cases.json VERIFY=1 JOBS=<J>` one after another on 22 cores, `/tmp/claude-1000/-diagram/c6fd72d1-ab6c-4736-b723-0697a1f5ca51/scratchpad/t173/measure.log`). Four is the best on this host, past it the sides' own time growing, which docs/diff-run.md records.
   - A JOBS of 0, a non-number or a missing value is refused with the fix; one above the owed sides is clamped.
