### T237 (T234: a change to a Rust stage's drawing owed no glyph-check until an Occasions line declared it by hand)

- **Approach**: `reviews owed` reads the Rust engines' drawing code item by item at the base and now (`rust/gate/crates/reviews/src/reviews/owed/redrawn.rs`); an item whose comment-free tokens differ is changed, and owes the glyph-check of each element it redraws, on the first map of its engine's kind that draws it (the declared route's choice, so the two share a slug and merge), with no size-audit. A draw function (it takes the writer `Svg`) redraws the kinds it names - the hamlet driver's read by line, each changed line the `svg.kind("...")` named last above it; the Mode A compound's marks whole, their `data-kind="..."` with what the draw functions they call draw (`buildings` calls `building`, `parts` calls `well`) - and one naming none and calling none its caller's; a writer method, helper or constant what its uses redraw (a use is its name called or read in another item, a free function's call never a method's of the same name; a writer method reaching no element is the document, every mark); a roll (it makes the writer) line by line, a line not touching the writer the stages' plumbing and nothing; a type, import or test nothing. Where the elements cannot be told (a kind chosen at run time, a line above a draw function's first kind, a mark past a draw call), each engine map's whole legend is owed, each element once, and the occasion says so. A map's legend is its drawing now, else its drawing at the base, so the unit stands when the change left the hamlet not current. The drawing code is: the hamlet driver, `rust/phases/src/driver.rs` and `driver/` (tests aside), drawing the live hamlets; the Mode A compound engine, `rust/mode_a/src/compound.rs`, `compound/emit.rs`, `compound/emit_parts.rs`, drawing the generated compounds (measured 2026-11-20 (grep of `Svg::default`, `Svg::new`, `.kind(` and `data-kind=` over `rust/`, tests aside): the stages under `rust/phases/src/` name no kind and touch no writer, `compound::sheet` is the one `emit::Svg::new` outside tests, and a hand sheet's marks are its `.svg`, already in `CODE`). On T234's own commit the lookup owes `glyph-check--sluice-gate--kuwabata` alone, merged with its declared line (measured 2026-11-20 (`reviews owed --units --landing` in a scratch clone at 7a3116d24, `origin/main` at its parent, main's mirror drawings beside it)); read whole, `draw_polder`'s deleted square owed the three live hamlets' whole legends besides, 18 units more (measured 2026-11-20 (the same run before draw functions were read by line)). A token-changing line in each of the driver's 55 non-drawing functions (`plan.rs`, `spec.rs`, `toe.rs`, `check.rs`, `record.rs`, `seeds.rs`, `driver.rs`, `polder.rs`, one at a time) owes nothing for 48, the sluice gate for `sluice_channel` and `sluice_frame`, and the whole legend for the five that pick a kind or an ink (`crop_ink`, `paddy_kind`, `fill`, `dike_kind`, `crown_fill`) (measured 2026-11-20 (a script inserting `let _t237 = 0;` after each function's opening brace in the scratch clone, `origin/main` at 7a3116d24, `reviews owed --units --landing` after each)); before the free-function rule, `toe.rs`'s `grow` owed the whole legend through the writer's `self.grow` (the same sweep). Now: the face is the outer face's own corners that stand nearest the flank (of the box round the dike), in order along the axis, carried one corner on round the dike's corner and out to the box's corner, so the strip meets the dike point for point, meets the next flank's strip at the corner's diagonal, and never turns onto the next face (the 32 bins and `BINS` gone); each straight reach of the feeder and the outfall has its bed (its drawn width, carried half a width past each end so a bend's corner is covered) taken out of the strip along the bed's own four sides (`difference`, a Weiler and Atherton walk of the strip's ring against the convex bed), so the reeds run to each bank of a slanting reach as of a square one and round a reach's end where it stops inside the strip; a bed reaching either end of the strip's span ends its run past the dike's end square across at the bed's nearest point past the dike's extent; and a piece wholly past the dike's own extent, the run past a corner the channel cuts off, is dropped. A first version boxed each reach's bed square to the map's axes and cut or bit the strip by that box (a CONVENTION the claims check judged MISLABELED, since a reader sees the bare ground beside a slanting bank): a reach 30 degrees off square across the 280 ft foot strip left the reeds 156 ft along the strip from its nearest bank at worst, and a reach 45 degrees off square ending inside the strip 56 ft (measured 2026-11-20 (the new test `the_reeds_reach_each_bank_of_a_slanting_channel` against the boxing stage, `make rust-test CRATE=rust/phases`)); now 0.5 ft, the test's sampling step, on both (measured 2026-11-20 (the same test, green)). ### T238 (T237: a Rust stage's placement change owed no review and refused nothing, where the deleted Python's placement code owed its declaration; T239: a declaration naming no element became a unit on no map)

- **Approach**: the old pattern owed no unit for a placement change by itself: `CODE` (`l7r/**/*.py` outside `ci/`, a pool map's `.gen.py` or `.svg`) refused the push until an active feature had an `## Occasions` section or a commit an `Occasion:` line, and a declared `placement-changed:` owed the element's glyph-check (observed 2026-11-20, method: `git show 0d65d0600:rust/gate/crates/reviews/src/reviews/owed.rs` and `git show 8942a2628^:scripts/reviews/review_owed.py`, `_CODE` and `check_declared`); `docs/reviews.md`'s occasions agree: an engine change moving things under rules already judged owes nothing, an element re-placed by substantially different rules owes its glyph-check, declared (observed 2026-11-20, method: its occasions table and "The declaration"). The Rust engines are now held to the same refusal (`owed/redrawn/placed.rs`, read by `touched_code`): a STAGE file - a `.rs` under `rust/phases/src/` or `rust/mode_a/src/compound/` that is no engine's drawing file and no test file, 45 files (measured 2026-11-20 (`find rust/phases/src rust/mode_a/src/compound -name '*.rs'`, 64 files, less the 8 whose names hold `tests` and the 11 drawing files `ENGINES` names, `driver.rs`, `driver/`, `compound/emit.rs` and `emit_parts.rs`)) - whose non-test items' comment-free tokens changed, and an engine drawing file with a changed function or constant whose change redraws no element (`redraws`' silent part: the item whole, or a changed line read by line - a roll's line handing the stages their ground, a mark under the placeholder `-`), refuse undeclared; a comment, a test, an import, a type or a file only moved does not; a change that redraws an element still owes its glyph-check from the change and asks nothing. A `tasks.md` declaration naming no element, map, sheet or reason, and one naming no known occasion (an unknown kind was a problem line only, wider than the task's no-element case), now owes no unit and is refused with its form by `--check-declared`, whatever code the delta touches, and the check reads no legend (the declarations' words, and the pool's folder names where a line names a map); a tweak's `Occasion:` commit line so formed owes no unit and is a problem line, never refused, since a commit message cannot be rewritten and the refusal could not be met, and a commit line with nothing after its colon declares nothing, as before. Measured undeclared, each commit in a scratch clone with `origin/main` at its parent and every touched feature's `## Occasions` section stripped: T239's dc9adbc94 refused nothing and owed nothing before, now refused naming `rust/phases/src/driver/polder.rs`, owing nothing (measured 2026-11-20 (`reviews owed --check-declared` and `--units --landing`, the binary before and after)); T236's 0f7583f1b refused nothing before, now names `driver/polder.rs` and `waterward.rs`, its comment-only `field/dike.rs` not named (measured 2026-11-20 (the same)); T234's 7a3116d24 owed `glyph-check--sluice-gate--kuwabata` and refused nothing before, and owes the same and refuses nothing now (measured 2026-11-20 (the same, the final binary)); a first version read a type as placement and refused it naming `driver/polder.rs`, its one silent item the new `SluiceFrame` only the frame's drawing fills (measured 2026-11-20 (a temporary probe test printing each silent item, removed)), so a type is no placement by itself; T239's silent items are the new helper `off_the_dike` and lines of `roll_polder`, T236's `stage_waterward` and the deleted `STRIP_CUT_HW` (measured 2026-11-20 (the same probe)). `--check-declared` on this clone took 37 to 48 ms against 55 to 63 ms before round 2 (measured 2026-11-20 (four runs each, wall time, the binary before and after)); after round 2 it takes 78 to 86 ms against 34 to 37 ms (measured 2026-11-20 (four runs each, wall time, the round-1 binary and the round-2 one, both through `l7r-gate.sh` with `L7R_GATE_STALE_OK=1`)), the difference the delta's code read (`touched_code`), which 449's section had let it skip: the old speed was the defect below.

### T238 Approach (checklist part A)

1. **The goal, in the world.** A change that re-places an element is judged by the glyph-check its feature declares, whether the placer is Python or Rust, so a moved element never ships unjudged for want of a line nobody was asked to write; and every declared line owes a review someone can run.
2. **The constraints.** Feature 294's occasions (`docs/reviews.md`: a re-placement by substantially different rules owes its glyph-check, declared; a change under rules already judged owes nothing); T237's detection of drawing changes kept; feature 444 FR-023 (hamlet units set aside at rust-only, recorded by T232's `dev/deferred-reviews.jsonl`); constitution XIV.
3. **Where each comes from.** G: feature 294's and 444's request words; R: `docs/reviews.md`; O: the old pattern read from git history, T237's and T239's findings and this task's measurements.
4. **Do they describe the world here?** Yes: measured on three real Rust commits undeclared (above), and in a scratch gate run - a scratch mirror holding main's drawings, a clone under its `.clones/` whose `origin/main` holds this task's code, and one commit on top widening the field grave's mound in `draw_field`, no Occasions line: `--check-declared` returns 0, the review gate at rust-only names `glyph-check--field-grave--inashiro` (its occasion "'field grave' is redrawn: the hamlet driver's drawing code changed (rust/phases/src/driver.rs draw_field)"), sets it aside, records it in `dev/deferred-reviews.jsonl` (no field-grave row before, one after) and commits it, and says clean (observed 2026-11-20, method: `review-gate.sh` with this task's final gate binary, `GUARD_LOG_DIR` in scratch, 36 s, most of it redrawing the fresh tree's maps). The maps were redrawn by this clone's prebuilt hamlet engine, so the widened mound itself was never compiled: the unit is read from the code's change, the legend from the drawing, and a mound's width changes no element of the census. That run's engine being prebuilt is the scratch set-up's, not the gate's: the launcher takes a binary as fresh by its time against its sources' (`scripts/gates/l7r-gate.sh`'s `stale`), so a binary seeded into a scratch target after the checkout reads as their build. A real landing's redraw builds the delta's own engine: `review-gate.sh` redraws each map not current by `cd "$ROOT" && make -s map MAP="$at"` (its line 193), the very `make map` the round-2 passage above ran by hand, which runs `l7r-gate pool map` with the launcher that builds (`pool/src/lib.rs`'s `cli`, `Launcher { build: true }`), and that hand-run `make map` rebuilt the hamlet driver from an edited source and drew the edit (measured 2026-11-20, round 2's D9c passage); the gate's own redraw is read, not measured end to end here (observed 2026-11-20, method: `review-gate.sh` lines 180-219, the Makefile's `map` target, `pool/src/lib.rs` and `cache/engine.rs`), a scratch gate run with an engine edit costing a scratch mirror and a fresh build of the gate.

### T242 (spec-fidelity's British form of 'behavior' in a decision id landed in plan-review.json three times on 2026-11-20, each turning `make quick` red and refusing a landing)

- **Approach**: every recorder that writes a reviewer's words into the repository writes them in the house style the push's delta check holds it to. `make plan-verdict`'s writer (`plan/record.rs`'s `house_style`) styled each decision's free text but wrote its `id` as given (`KEPT` held it with the digests, as "what the gate matches on"), and nothing compares an id - `status.rs` names a BLOCKED one and the arbiter's bundle prints it (observed 2026-11-20, method: `grep` of `"id"` over `rust/` and `scripts/`, `review_round_hooks.rs`'s `plan_rounds` reading blocks alone). The guard's `americanize` holds a straight-quoted `"..."` span as a quotation, which suits a prose file, but the delta check (`checks/house_style_delta.rs`) holds straight quotes only in a `.md`, `.html` or `.txt` file: a JSON record's straight-quoted British word is flagged (measured 2026-11-20 (a scratch git repository holding one untracked `r.json`, `l7r-gate check house-style-delta` on it: the plain and the straight-quoted word flagged, 2 findings, the curly-quoted and backticked ones held)). So the guard gains `americanize_record` (the same correction holding only what the delta check holds in a non-prose file: code spans, 「」, 『』, curly quotes, `<q>`, `<blockquote>`) and `americanize_json` (every string of a JSON value through it, keys as written), and each JSON recorder uses them: `make plan-verdict` (every string of each decision, the id and nested lists too), `make arbiter-ruled` (its own `house_styled` replaced), `make claims-checked` (each verdict note and UNCLAIMED decision), `make gm-escalated` (escalation-check's reason) and a GM question (`gm_review::question`, the arbiter's `for_gm` among its callers), and `make record-checked`'s OUTSIDE THE CHANGE findings into `found.jsonl` (each finding; its file and block as given, they name things); the ledger's row filled from an agent's reply (`make ledger-owed WRITE=`, a landing's cheap pass) takes `americanize` on its first line, the ledger being Markdown, styled before the 110-character cut.

### T162 (a guard defect T147's port agent met: its own clone refused by the session that launched it)

- **Approach**: the clone-sync guard (`rust/guard/src/guards/clone_sync_hooks.rs`) lets a session through the clone its dispatcher claims; the dispatcher was only `L7R_DISPATCHER`, which a page session's runner sets. A background job Claude Code starts from an interactive session runs as `--fork-session --resume <the parent's transcript>`, the parent stays live and claims the same clone, and nothing named it, so the job's first write was refused as a second live session in the tree. With no `L7R_DISPATCHER`, the guard now reads the session's own process arguments (the sessions json's pid, its `/proc` command line) and takes the session it was forked from as its dispatcher.

   **Decisions** (constitution XIV, a defect fixed where it was found; FR-001's guards ported in phase 1, whose behavior this extends):
   - Found where: T147's agent was refused on its first write into this session's clone, `already occupied by another live session` naming this session's own parent, and wrote through a copy from scratch instead; this session's process runs as `--fork-session --resume <the parent's transcript>`, and the parent's process is live (observed 2026-11-16, method: the sessions json and `/proc` of both processes).
   - Only a fork counts: a session resumed without `--fork-session` is the same conversation continued, not a launched job, and it stays refused beside a live claimant; the resumed argument's leaf, less `.jsonl`, is the parent's id.
   - The exemption is the one a page session already has (the dispatcher's claim alone is let through); every other live claimant still refuses.
   - The checks: the guard's tests green with a test holding a forked session through and an unforked one refused, the test failing with the fix taken out, and the guard's line coverage complete (observed 2026-11-16, method: `make rust-test CRATE=rust/guard`, run with and without the fix, and `l7r-gate.sh rust uncovered --crate rust/guard`).

### T122 (the full hook run's wall time, the GM's pre-approval of 2026-11-12: a concrete target with a measured saving)

- **Approach**: the full hook run (`make hooks-test HOOKS_ALL=1`) cut by its three bounds together: the idle-tests suite's real-time waits in fractions of a second (the guard's fixture seams `IDLE_WAIT_S` and `IDLE_DEFER_S`, `rust/guard/src/guards/idle_tests_hooks.rs`, honored inside a fixture alone, and `tests/hooks/test-idle-tests-hooks.sh`), the entry-gate suite's fixture answering its units a check at a time (`tests/hooks/test-entry-gate.sh`), and the Makefile's missing-program self-test started beside the suites instead of after them.

   **Decisions** (the GM's pre-approval in `request.md`, "a fifth efficiency round"; FR-002 for every suite case; docs/performance-checklist.md):
   - Why it did not land on 2026-11-12: the idle-tests change alone cut that suite from 35.0 s to about 17 s (observed 2026-11-12, method: T122's first runs, its note in tasks.md), but the full run did not move, because the next suites bounded it - entry-gate, its fixture answering eleven units with one call each where each `record-owed` call rebuilds the tree's owed units - and about 8 s ran outside any suite, the self-test serial after them (observed 2026-11-17, method: the run's own step times, `/tmp/claude-1000/-diagram/c6fd72d1-ab6c-4736-b723-0697a1f5ca51/scratchpad/t122/runs.txt`). Back-to-back runs on this host also drive the CPU to 94 °C and slow the CPU-bound suites about 1.5 times, which hid the gain (observed 2026-11-17, method: the package temperature and the load logged beside each run, `/tmp/claude-1000/-diagram/c6fd72d1-ab6c-4736-b723-0697a1f5ca51/scratchpad/t122/runs.txt`).
   - The changes, every case and check kept: entry-gate's fixture answers notes a question at a time, other subjects by kind and the three modal units as one modal-research answer, as a session records them - three calls in place of eleven, the same units answered, its case 4 still proving the gate falls quiet; the self-test's pass, failure and stamp are read after the suites as before, a plain `make hooks-test` still skipping it when unchanged.
   - Before and after, each run started cool: the full run took 43.0, 43.3 and 43.4 s before and 29.4, 28.8 and 29.0 s after (observed 2026-11-17, method: `/tmp/claude-1000/-diagram/c6fd72d1-ab6c-4736-b723-0697a1f5ca51/scratchpad/t122/runs.txt`, each run started under 60 °C and a one-minute load under 3, `/tmp/claude-1000/-diagram/c6fd72d1-ab6c-4736-b723-0697a1f5ca51/scratchpad/t122/full.sh`). Alone, idle-tests went from 34.8 to 17.0 s and entry-gate from 22.8 to 13.5 s (observed 2026-11-17, method: `/tmp/claude-1000/-diagram/c6fd72d1-ab6c-4736-b723-0697a1f5ca51/scratchpad/t122/runs.txt`, each run started under 60 °C and a one-minute load under 3, `/tmp/claude-1000/-diagram/c6fd72d1-ab6c-4736-b723-0697a1f5ca51/scratchpad/t122/full.sh`). Back to back on a hot CPU the run took about 62 s before and 53 to 55 s after (observed 2026-11-17, method: `/tmp/claude-1000/-diagram/c6fd72d1-ab6c-4736-b723-0697a1f5ca51/scratchpad/t122/runs.txt`, runs started without waiting to cool), the figure a gate after builds sees.
   - The next bound, recorded and not cut: sync-with-main, with entry-gate and l7r-gate within 4 s of it (observed 2026-11-17, method: the after runs' suite times, `/tmp/claude-1000/-diagram/c6fd72d1-ab6c-4736-b723-0697a1f5ca51/scratchpad/t122/runs.txt`), so a further cut needs all three; its candidates are sync-with-main's system time, `record-owed`'s fixed cost a call, l7r-gate's real browser and model starts, and `deps --keys` serial before the suites.
   - The checks: `make static` green, `make rust-test` green, `make hooks-test HOOKS_ALL=1` green on 54 suites (observed 2026-11-17, method: those commands, one after another after the last edit).

### T122 Approach (checklist part A)

1. **The goal, in the world.** The full hook run waits only as long as its cases need.
2. **The constraints.** FR-002: every case and check held; the GM's condition, a measured saving.
3. **Where each comes from.** G: the GM's pre-approval; O: the runs T122 recorded (its record removed on landing, in git history).
4. **Do they describe the world here?** Measured on this host cool and hot, measured 2026-11-17 (`/tmp/claude-1000/-diagram/c6fd72d1-ab6c-4736-b723-0697a1f5ca51/scratchpad/t122/runs.txt`).
5. **The order.** After T160, which found the run's bound.
6. **The exits.** Green: `make static`, `make rust-test`, `make hooks-test HOOKS_ALL=1` and `make land` green. Red: what failed recorded and the task set down, a claim that it cannot be done ruled through `make arbiter-ask`.
7. **The search smell.** None.
8. **The budget.** One landing.
9. **Done, measured.** The full run a third faster from a cool start.
10. **Before moving a constant.** None moved.
11. **Before fitting things into room.** Not a room question.

**Performance work?** Yes, of the hook suites: (1) the time went to idle-tests' real waits, entry-gate's eleven `record-owed` calls and the serial self-test, measured per suite; (2) each change removes work or waiting; (3) the expected saving was the bound's, about a third; (4) the run is bounded by its longest suite, so the next cut needs the three now level; (5) before and after started cool, and hot, the temperature and load stated; (6) no map moved.

### T161 (the GM's second approved proposal, the differentials rerunning only what a fix touched, enforced by tooling; request.md 2026-11-16, the GM 2026-11-11)

- **Approach**: one shared differential runner in the repository, `l7r-gate diff-run <cases file>` (a new gate crate, Rust as all new tooling is under FR-001), which every port task's comparison uses from T147 on in place of a hand-written driver loop: it runs each case on both sides, compares, records, and after a fix reruns only the cases whose key moved.

   **Decisions** (the GM's words in request.md, 2026-11-16 and 2026-11-11; FR-002, whose proof the runner carries; `ask:449-T159-rounds`, which filed it):
   - Why: the differential is the part of a port task's time a script can cut. T145's agent waited on its harness 53.8 min in the background and 10.1 min in the foreground of a 232 min run, and T143's 20.9 min and 9.2 min of a 100 min run (observed 2026-11-16, method: each tool call's and background run's wait in the agents' transcripts, `/tmp/claude-1000/-diagram/c6fd72d1-ab6c-4736-b723-0697a1f5ca51/scratchpad/agent_time.py`); each of those runs reran every case after each fix, the hand-written drivers keeping no record of what a case had already shown.
   - The shape is the one the hand-written harnesses of T143 to T146 share, so a port's harness moves onto it without losing a case: a world built per side (a setup command run into a fresh directory), the two sides as command templates over that world, each case's steps, the outputs compared (exit, stdout, stderr, every file the case wrote under the world, named extra files such as a server's log), named normalizations (a regex and its replacement, each listed in the report as taken), and one results row a case.
   - Each side of a case is kept on its own key, so a fix to the port reruns what it could change and nothing else: the old side's key is the hash of the case's definition, its normalizations, the content of the inputs it declares and the old side's fingerprint (the files it runs from, the Python tree at its revision), so a fix to the port never moves it and the old side's recorded result stands across every rerun of a task; the new side's key is the same with, in place of the whole binary, the content of the source paths the case declares it exercises (a crate's directory, say), so a fix reruns the new side of the cases whose declared sources it touched. A case that declares no sources keys its new side on the whole new-side fingerprint, as a rebuild then reruns it. Because a declaration can be too narrow, the figures a plan reports come from `--verify`, one run of every case's new side at the end against the kept old sides, which the report names as a verify run; `--only <name>` reruns one case.
   - Noise is the runner's too: `--twice` runs the old side twice and reports what differs between the two runs, the evidence that a normalization covers run-to-run noise and nothing more (T146's harness did this by hand).
   - Enforced by tooling, as the GM's 2026-11-11 words ask: the runner makes the incremental rerun its default; `--all`, which reruns every side of every case, takes a `REASON=` of two words or more and records it in the report and the guard log, as the gate's escapes do (FR-011); and `make decide`'s lint refuses a sentence stating a differential's case count (`cases` beside `differential` or FR-002's `same outputs`) that cites no runner verify report - the path `--verify` writes, which carries `diff-run-verify` in its name, a report of an incremental run not counting - in any feature's plan, so a port whose comparison ran through a hand-written loop cannot reach its review with that figure.
   - Out of scope: what a world needs beyond a setup command (a network namespace, a loopback server, a bare remote) stays the harness's setup script, which the runner runs and keys.

### T161 Approach (checklist part A)

1. **The goal, in the world.** A port's differential reruns after a fix only the cases the fix could change, through one runner every port uses.
2. **The constraints.** The GM's words (request.md, 2026-11-16 and 2026-11-11); FR-002, whose comparison it carries; FR-001 and FR-004 (new tooling in Rust, full line coverage).
3. **Where each comes from.** G: the GM's approval and his enforcement rule; O: the transcript split above; R: the four hand-written harnesses whose shape it takes.
4. **Do they describe the world here?** The shape read from T143's to T146's harnesses, measured 2026-11-16 (`/tmp/claude-1000/-diagram/c6fd72d1-ab6c-4736-b723-0697a1f5ca51/scratchpad/agent_time.py`).
5. **The order.** After T159; before T147, whose differential is its first user.
6. **The exits.** Green: the crate's tests and coverage - among them a case whose input moved rerun and one whose did not kept, a change to one declared source rerunning only the new side of the cases declaring it with every old side kept, `--verify` rerunning every new side, `--all` refused without a reason, and the lint refusing a differential count with no runner report - and `make land` green. Red: what failed recorded and the task set down, a claim that it cannot be done ruled through `make arbiter-ask`.
7. **The search smell.** None.
8. **The budget.** One landing.
9. **Done, measured.** The crate's tests, and T147's runner reports counting, after each fix, the sides it reran and the sides it kept, its figures from a verify run.
10. **Before moving a constant.** None moved.
11. **Before fitting things into room.** Not a room question.

**Performance work?** No - it saves an agent's waiting on reruns, not the tools' running time.

Worked by two agents in turn: part A the libraries, part B the wiring and the differential.

   **Decisions** (`ask:449-engine-order` conditions 2, 3 and 5, `ask:449-phase4-slices` Q10, `ask:449-usage-text`, FR-001 to FR-005, FR-008; the GM's words, request.md 2026-11-17):

Its largest difference from GEOS over every red fixture's half-hour steps is 1.99e-4 px2 against a nearest margin to a threshold of 25.3 px2, so no verdict can turn on it, and the test asserts the difference stays under the margin (observed 2026-11-18, method: both computed on 882 half-hour steps, `/tmp/claude-1000/-diagram/c6fd72d1-ab6c-4736-b723-0697a1f5ca51/scratchpad/t175/a/phases.log` line 14; the landed test measures the garden's red fixture's 210 steps).
   - Claims (Q10): the claims on the kept `.py` units stay keyed to them; each Rust copy carries its claim word for word where it describes the Rust, or a claim stating what the Rust unit decides where a memo, a regex range or a figure moved; every other new unit carries its module's NONE; `py.rs`'s module claim is widened to its arithmetic, as two claims rounds asked. `make claims-owed` owes 434 new claims in 25 files one impl-drift round and 11 a triage (observed 2026-11-18, method: `make claims-owed`).
   - The same outputs (FR-002): HEAD's `make pack-audit` against the Rust on each pool sheet, all of them in one call, every fixture sheet where it lies and under its tier with its notes, 17 notes and manifest forms, 12 file refusals and the argument forms, directly and through make - the differential's 207 cases, none differing, every pool case exiting 0 with its full report on both sides (measured 2026-11-18 (`make diff-run CASES=/tmp/claude-1000/-diagram/c6fd72d1-ab6c-4736-b723-0697a1f5ca51/scratchpad/t175/b/diff/cases.json VERIFY=1 JOBS=4`, `/tmp/claude-1000/-diagram/c6fd72d1-ab6c-4736-b723-0697a1f5ca51/scratchpad/t175/b/diff/cases.diff-run/reports/diff-run-verify-20261118T033436Z.json`)). Normalizations: a traceback's frames, and an uncaught `JSONDecodeError` or `UnicodeDecodeError` message compared by its class, under `ask:449-usage-text`'s clause leaving an uncaught traceback's text unbound while the exit and stdout stay bound. The usage line both sides print still names `python3 -m ...pack_audit`: it is bound output, kept as T170 kept its own.

### T180 (the GM 2026-11-18, request.md: no exactness standard for a port)

- **Approach**: the living guidance amended to the GM's rule - an output may differ from what it replaces so long as everything works: its tests pass, it does its job for its callers, its research claims hold - and, as FR-002 states it, neither an exactness standard: a drawn output passes its checks and holds its research claims, and a ported check still does its job (its red fixtures still fail, what it passed still passes), a check fixed or improved on purpose changing as fixed (restated 2026-11-21 by the plan review of 449's changed blocks, `/tmp/sfr449/verdict.json`, to the GM's 2026-11-18 words: "surely you mean \"the audit checks must pass\" right?!"). The constitution (2.35.0: Principle XIII's "A differing output is not a regression", X's clause 15 widened), its plan, spec and phase templates and the speckit-specify checklist; spec.md's FR-002 (its byte-only ruled cases collapsed into the rule, the three that set a verdict or a behavior kept), its phase-4 paragraph, FR-012 and SC-007; engine-plan.md ("What the same means for any port", condition 3's lockstep restated: a test may show agreement, bytes are not required); the root and three subtree CLAUDE.md files; docs/efficiency-tooling.md, spec-kit-and-reviews.md, diff-run.md (a difference a signal, not a bar) and gm-rulings.md (the GM's words); dev/performance.md; and the review agents' files - spec-fidelity, spec-fidelity-verify, round-arbiter and escalation-check - which launch without CLAUDE.md, so each carries the rule and the GM's words: a reviewer never blocks, narrows or sends back a port for differing bytes, and a requirement demanding byte agreement is itself the finding.

   **Decisions** (the GM's words, request.md 2026-11-18 and 2026-11-17; docs/efficiency-tooling.md, 2026-10-18):
   - Kept, as not a port's exactness standard: reproducibility (the same code and seed give the same map; the cache audit; counters that must not change a map), a lossless split's integrity, a file hash naming its content, and the research rule that a quotation is verbatim; past specs and dated records, history, left as written.
   - Held, not kept exact, as the GM's "everything works" is judged by it: the audit checks pass, a ported check still does its job (its red fixtures fail, what it passed still passes), and a check fixed or improved on purpose changes as fixed (FR-002).
   - The rule is applied from here on: finished tasks' plan sections stay as the records of what they measured, and `rust/mode_a`'s lockstep tests stay until a harmless difference makes one fail, when it is changed to hold the verdicts and claims (engine-plan.md's restated condition 3).
   - The checks: `make hooks-test HOOKS_ALL=1` and the pointer check green (observed 2026-11-18, method: those commands after the last edit, `/tmp/claude-1000/-diagram/c6fd72d1-ab6c-4736-b723-0697a1f5ca51/scratchpad/t180/hooks.log`, `/tmp/claude-1000/-diagram/c6fd72d1-ab6c-4736-b723-0697a1f5ca51/scratchpad/t180/pointers.log`); `make static` red only on T151's port in progress (three uncalled functions in `rust/mode_a/src/labels/`, `/tmp/claude-1000/-diagram/c6fd72d1-ab6c-4736-b723-0697a1f5ca51/scratchpad/t180/static.log`), run again green at the landing with T151's work committed. The sweep's search is `/tmp/claude-1000/-diagram/c6fd72d1-ab6c-4736-b723-0697a1f5ca51/scratchpad/t180/sweep-grep.txt`, its hits after the amendment `/tmp/claude-1000/-diagram/c6fd72d1-ab6c-4736-b723-0697a1f5ca51/scratchpad/t180/sweep-grep-after.txt`.

### T203 (T202's plan review came back NOT-REVIEWABLE on a heading's `704x its SOUND derived budget` with no label, and T209's on `moved five captions a few pixels`: the figure lint passed both)

- **Approach**: the lint's whole-section rules already read a heading line - `SPLIT_UNIT` and `SPLIT_SENTENCE` cut at a line opening with `#`, and a heading such as `### T05 (183 lines)` is refused today (observed 2026-11-22, method: the count rule's test over that heading, green on the old lint) - so what let T202's heading through was its figure's form: `704x` is a figure to no rule, the unit pattern holding no `x` and item 4's bare-figure pattern refusing a digit run followed by a letter. So `rust/gate/crates/plan/src/plan/lint.rs` reads a multiple written close (`704x`, `100x-4,400x`) as a figure with a unit, everywhere the unit rule reads, the heading among them, and item 4's bare figure takes the `x` too; a rule's multiple (`past 2x`, `more than 2x`, `the 2x rule`, `the 2x raise`) is a limit and no figure, and a spaced `2 x 3` is arithmetic or a size and no multiple. A count spelled as a word (`two` to `twenty`, the tens, `hundred(s)`, `thousand(s)`, `dozen(s)`; never `one`, which names) is read by the count rule where a counted noun follows, as a numeral is, and the count nouns gain `captions`; a threshold's word (`at most ten keys`) stays a limit. Item 4's any-number rule does not take the words: on the first replay they added 45 item-4 findings, nearly all naming ("the three checks", "the two places") (measured 2026-11-22 (T203's replay of `findings` over every task section of `specs/*/plan.md` and `plan-done.md`, old lint against new)). The refusals' words name both forms. Red first: the new tests `a_multiple_needs_a_label_in_a_heading_as_in_the_approach` (T202's heading) and `a_count_spelled_as_a_word_needs_a_label` (T209's sentence) both fail on the old lint (measured 2026-11-22 (`make rust-test CRATE=rust/gate/crates/plan` in a detached worktree of HEAD with the new tests copied in: 2 failed, 167 passed)).
- **The replay**: every task section of `specs/*/plan.md` and `plan-done.md` through the old and the new lint gave 1547 and 1760 findings, 213 new and 0 gone, every new one a count spelled as a word and no new multiple (measured 2026-11-22 (a temporary test calling `findings` per `##`/`###` task block in both trees, its rows sorted and compared with `comm`; the rows kept in `/tmp/t203/replay-new-findings.tsv`)). Of the 213 new findings 203 are in closed sections - 65 of 449, 55 of 451, 28 of 405, 17 of 385, 11 of 444, the rest across 374, 417, 418, 420, 422, 423 and 435 - and are reported, not fixed; 10 are in open tasks' sections, reported to their owners and not fixed here, since each label is a measurement only its task's run can give and 449 T158's section is its builder's, mid-edit (measured 2026-11-22 (the same rows, each placed under its block's task and that task's box in its `tasks.md`)):
  - 417 T21 (plan.md:1136), `SC-006's two test landings`;
  - 417 T66 (plan.md:1251 and 1255), `the last three sites` and `a few hundred thousand calls`;
  - 444 T27 (plan.md:576, 579 and 682) and 444 T34 (plan.md:1109), `the two rows` and `the four files' run`;
  - 449 T158 (plan.md:378 and 382), `those two crates`, `its two cases`;
  - 449 T244 (plan.md:909), `three tests in phase_source_hooks/tests.rs`.

| step | alone off: fixed and pinned | fresh block vs HEAD | pool manifests moved | the last resort |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| the multiple and the number words | `lint/tests.rs`'s two new tests | n/a (a gate lint, no map) | none | none |

### T216 (T212's log, 2026-11-19: a first coverage run after the lockstep deletion seemed to name 5 lines, the next hundreds - observed 2026-11-19, method: T212's `make static` output in its transcript)

- **Approach**: no code change - not a defect (constitution XIV: a defect is a wrong outcome, not a difference). The coverage run named every uncovered line both times; T212's own command showed it only the last three files (measured 2026-11-22 (the replay and transcript below)). Measured three ways:
  - **Lead 1, the replay** - measured 2026-11-22 (T212's 86 timestamped tool calls up to its 18:10:06Z `make static`, read from its transcript `c6fd72d1.../subagents/agent-a9ff219aabc9012c9.jsonl` and run again in a worktree at its parent `443e0f8113`, with T212's own tool, `scripts/gates/l7r-gate.sh rust cover --crate rust/mode_a`):
    - The 18:10:06 tree's first coverage run names 20 files and 668 lines (measured 2026-11-22 (`grep -c` of the replayed run's log, `/tmp/t216x/s1810.log`)).
    - Its `audit/checks.rs` lines (133, 143, 144, 436, 472, 484) and `audit/labels.rs` lines (33-43, 53, 54, 61-64, 106-113, 115, 144, 145) are the ones T212's 18:12:00 run printed.
    - The previous builder's replay was a different state: the final tree with `check_fixtures` unwired, not the 18:10:06 tree.
  - **Why T212 saw 5** - measured 2026-11-22 (its 18:10:06 command, read from the transcript, against the replayed log):
    - The command was `grep -iE "^error|warning:|FAILED|uncovered|dead code|refus|Diff in" static.log | head -40; tail -6 static.log`.
    - The tool prints each file as `<path> - lines no test reaches: ...`, so no pattern matched a file line.
    - `tail -6` showed the last three files alphabetically: `parse/shapes.rs` 61, 86; `pool_sweep.rs` 404; `tagged.rs` 98, 327 (measured 2026-11-22 (`tail -6` of the replayed log beside T212's printed output)). That is exactly the "5 lines" of the task line (measured 2026-11-22 (the same comparison)).
    - T212's 18:12:00 command added `lines no test` to its pattern and saw them all.
    - So the 5-line reading was right for its code only as a tail: the report itself was whole.
  - **Lead 2, a stale report** - measured 2026-11-22 (`cargo llvm-cov report` run directly over a planted `STALE` report file):
    - An empty profile directory exits 1 ("no input files").
    - A profile with no binary exits 1 ("No filenames specified!").
    - Both leave the old file in place, but `cover.rs`'s `missed` reads the report only when the run's code is 0. Either case fails the crate as line 0, never as a stale read.
  - **Lead 3, concurrent runs** - measured 2026-11-22 (the clone's `.git/l7r-events/*.jsonl`, every `make` Pre/Post pair 16:00-18:30Z on 2026-11-19):
    - Only T212's own runs ran, one at a time.
    - Its blocked 18:10:02 `make static` never started.
    - No run overlapped another.

### T241 (impl-drift on T239, 2026-11-20: off_the_dike's bundle held 0019 and 0081 while its claims cite 0027)

The 0081 of that bundle was another unit's page: T239's bundle held several units, and off_the_dike's own claims cite 0019 and 0027 alone (its unit bundled alone, measured 2026-11-22), so 0081 leaving is no loss.

- **Approach**: the claims bundle (`rust/gate/crates/claims/src/claims/bundle.rs`) gathered a unit's questions from its claims' parsed backings alone (`Claim.pointers`), and dropped a backing page that was not a file without a word. A claim's line can cite a page the grammar does not read as its backing: an account's `...; research/questions/<page>: ...`, or a `GUESS: research/questions/<page>: ...`, whose colon makes the page account and the backing a bare GUESS. off_the_dike's two claims cite 0027 both ways. The fix is `cited_pages`: the backing's pointers, then every `research/questions/NNNN-<id>[.drawing].html` the claim's line names (the grammar's own `POINTER` pattern), in order, once. Every one is bundled, and a page that is no question file refuses the bundle, naming the unit, the claim and the page. Each claim's `units.json` pages are its `cited_pages` too, where they were its pointers: `claims-checked` drops a reply's rests on a page not in them (`reply.rs`, "a page it does not cite - dropped"), so a verdict resting on a 0027 block would have lost that rest. Red first: `every_page_a_claim_cites_is_in_its_bundle_or_the_bundle_refuses_naming_it` (`bundle/tests.rs`). At HEAD it failed at its first assertion: the account-cited page was not bundled. Its refusal half names a page the record never had. The replay was measured 2026-11-22 (the builder over every claim of `dev/claims-index.json`, in four bundles of at most 900 keys; each gaining unit then bundled alone and its `questions/` diffed against its `units.json` pages, which are exactly the old page list):
  - 3,274 claims over 2,562 units bundled, and none refused, measured 2026-11-22 (the replay). Six index rows (measured 2026-11-22, the builder's `no such claim(s)` lists) name no current claim and were left out; they are the index's stale rows.
  - 63 units gain 72 pages, measured 2026-11-22 (the replay), for example `polder.rs::off_the_dike` +0027, `waterward.rs::pieces` +0019 +0027, `field/dike.rs::CROWN_FT` and `GAP_HALF_FT` +0027, `audit/sun.rs::NOT_STANDING` +0038 +0103 +0165, `compound.rs::sheet` +0090 +0092 +0242. The list is in the session's report.
  - Over those bundles' claim lines, 0 `research/questions/` mentions miss the pattern, and 0 pages are cited by a bare id, measured 2026-11-22 (a scan of every KEY line of the four MANIFESTs). "Every page" holds for the record as it stands.
  - `make claims-owed`'s set was empty, and `--owed` selected none.

### T244 (the GM 2026-11-21, docs/gm-rulings.md, its section Stop before homesteads, and talk first: "When you get to the point where you have ported everything else and then we're ready to go back to homesteads, then don't actually proceed. Why don't you go ahead and stop, and then we can talk more after everything else is done before you get started on that.")

- **Approach**: one shared reader, `rust/guard/shared/src/parked.rs` (the stages `rust/parked/src/` holds, read from the tree: homesteads, track, appurtenances, law, ways; a task's stage, its box line opening `phase: <stage>` or a `phase:` line of its block; the resumed record `<git common dir>/parked-resumed.jsonl`; the write and shell predicates; the ruling and the refusal), and four doors over it. (a) The source move and the `lib.rs` line: `rust/guard/src/guards/phase_source_hooks.rs`, its matcher widened to `Write|Edit|MultiEdit`, a parked arm run before the read hold's early returns - a Write, Edit or MultiEdit landing in `rust/phases/src/<stage>(.rs|/...)`, or putting a `mod <stage>` into `rust/phases/src/lib.rs` that the replaced text lacked, and a shell write the tree walk finds there (`mv`, `cp`, `rsync`, a redirect, `sed -i`; a `git mv`'s destination read from its last word, since the walk lands it where git runs), refused unless the stage is resumed. (b) The task-start: `rust/gate/crates/task/src/task_start.rs`'s `parked_stage`, before the performance-first check and before any file is written, so the session is told to stop, never to escape `PERF_LATER_OK`. (c) `GM_RESUMED="<the GM's words>"` is the escape: the gate checks its form (two words, recorded in the guard log as `parked-stage`, the stage then written to `parked-resumed.jsonl`), and the guard holds its words on a shell call - a move, or a `make task-start` - to a message the GM wrote this session (the approval line's test, `feature_approval_hooks::problem`, as `budget_change_hooks` holds `WORDS=`), so a session cannot resume a stage on words of its own; a heredoc body or a quoted argument naming `GM_RESUMED=` is no escape. (d) The set-down: `set_down_hooks`' two pickers and its fallback skip a held stage's task; with only those open, the Stop refusal names the ruling and `make set-down`, and `set_down.rs`'s `parked_stop` takes that set-down with no arbiter ruling and under the usage cap, its row carrying `ruling` and its reply naming it.
- **Which stage tasks are held**: the parked ones, not every 444 `phase:` task. 444's T27 (seat) and T29 (waterward) are stages already in `rust/phases/src/lib.rs`, open but not parked; the GM's words are "go back to homesteads", and `rust/parked/CLAUDE.md` names homesteads, track and appurtenances (with law and ways) as the parked ones. One predicate (`parked::held_task`), read from the tree, so a stage moved back is held no longer.
- **Measured before**, measured 2026-11-22 (a fixture clone `/tmp/t244-measure/c` holding 444's real `spec.md`, `plan.md` and its tasks.md with only T30-T33 and the GM review open, the Stop replayed through `tests/hooks/set-down-hooks.sh`, the set-down through `scripts/gates/l7r-gate.sh set-down 444` under the session's real cap reading): with nothing running the guard named `T30 phase: homesteads ... - performance work first, FR-013: make task-start F=444 T=T30`, with one agent running the free slot named `make task-start F=444 T=T30, then dispatch its builder`, and `make set-down` was refused with `the weekly cap is 100% and the 7-day figure is 64%`, measured 2026-11-22 (the same fixture). With T27 and T29 open too, both named T27 (seat), measured 2026-11-22 (the same fixture, its tasks.md with T27 and T29 open).
- **The replay** measured 2026-11-22 (`/tmp/t244-replay`, a scratch crate on this clone's `l7r_shared`, one process, 8.5 MB peak, 3.4 s): `parked::shell_hits` over the 9,646 Bash calls of T93's `/tmp/t93/replay-cmd.jsonl` (Bash calls only; the corpus holds no Write or Edit) - 0 hits, so 0 changed verdicts; one row names `GM_RESUMED=` (this task's own `make task-add TITLE="..."`), a quoted argument, which `parked::words` reads as no escape after the fix the replay found (it was a hit of `words` before; the guard's verdict on it was unchanged either way, since the row invokes `task-add`, not `task-start`, and moves nothing).

What it does, per 451's `plan-done.md` T142 section: rustc 1.87's incremental release with local ThinLTO can reuse one codegen unit's post-LTO object while the unit defining a symbol it imports is rebuilt under a new `.llvm.` name, so a crate's rlib holds an undefined symbol behind a fresh fingerprint; a `CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0` build is a separate artifact set and leaves the bad rlib for the next incremental build, which is why it came back. `scripts/gates/l7r-gate.sh` now reads each `<crate>-<meta>.<unit>.rcgu.o` the linker names, drops only that crate's incremental session holding the unit and its `.fingerprint/<crate>-<meta>` under cargo's own `.cargo-lock`, says what it dropped, and rebuilds once incrementally; a link error naming no unit rebuilds once with `CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0`; a second failure is refused with the cargo text. So the code is not against the record: on Sawada's declared fall the wind-facing margins lie on the wet toe, the seat takes the high, dry margin the page's first sentence gives, and the houses still face south by 0029's rule - the cluster's back to the hill is the one unrecorded choice, the algorithmically easier route the record leaves open. ### T252 (T228 found it, 2026-11-22; escalation-check KEEP; the GM ruled 2026-11-22, request.md "Constitution VI's one self-scoping command": "okay good, please proceed on that basis then")

- **Approach**: the GM's option A, built as the ruling says. Build the one self-scoping command over the Rust sweeps, keep Constitution VI's clause, and put the new command's name into the clause as upkeep, with no version. Since 444 T39 deleted the Python `mapcheck.py`, there have been two commands, `make map MAP=` and `make rust-test CRATE=rust/mode_a`, and the clause forbids two. `make maps` is that one command again: the name the clause already uses, and free since 449 T223 removed the target.
  - **The command.** `make maps [SCOPE=reference|all] [TIER=<row>]` runs `l7r-gate pool maps` (`rust/gate/crates/pool/src/maps.rs`), then `pool-index-if-stale` as `make map` does. It reads ONE record, `.git/maps-state.json` (per checkout: a worktree's `.git` file is followed, as `tree/src/state.rs` follows it), as the clause says ("One piece of state drives both the scope and the verbosity") and as `mapcheck.py` kept it (`.mapcheck.json`, read at `git show ea5638968e^:l7r/diagram/tools/mapcheck.py`). The rules follow the clause word for word:
    - **last run PASSED**: every row's whole run, every failure collected;
    - **last run FAILED, or no last run**: each row's reference map, stopping at the first problem; once every reference is clean, the same run widens to every row whole;
    - **`SCOPE=reference` / `SCOPE=all`**: says what is meant; `TIER=` runs one row.
    - **One record, not one per row**: a failure in any row narrows every row's next run. The cost is about half a second of references a row (measured below). A record per row was priced and not taken: it would change the clause's one-state rule.
  - **The tier table** (`TIERS` in `maps.rs`, one row a tier; a larger tier adds its row as it lands, as the clause says):
    - **`hamlets`** (folder `hamlets`). Reference: `inashiro` (the clause's canonical hamlet). The reference run is `pool map` plus `hamlet --check <spec>`. The whole run is `pool map` of every pool hamlet, `hamlet --check` of each, and `hamlet --cohort 1 48` (`make cohort`'s seeds).
    - **`mode-a`** (folders `magistracies`, `country-shrines`, every Mode A tier the building types declare with a pool folder). Reference: `county-magistracy-example`, a GENERATED compound, because the clause is about generator changes and a hand sheet does not move under one (the session approved it, 2026-11-22). The reference run is `pool map` plus `mode-a sweep <map>`. The whole run is `pool map` of every live Mode A map, then `rust test --crate rust/mode_a` (`make rust-test CRATE=rust/mode_a`'s: the crate's tests, 321 measured 2026-11-22 (`make rust-test CRATE=rust/mode_a`), the pool sweep among them, reused where nothing moved).
    - **Ordering**: the reference comes first in each whole run, so a narrow run is a prefix of a wide one (mapcheck's rule). Widening re-runs the references inside the whole runs, a cached draw and a judge, so no separate path is needed.
  - **Why the two judging commands.** A draw judges no rule, so the reference step needs a judge besides `make map`. Measured 2026-11-22 by reading `cache/draw.rs` and `rust/phases/src/bin/hamlet.rs`:
    - `pool map` fails a hamlet only on a non-zero exit, and the one-spec roll exits 0 with refusals and never asks `driver::check::check`; only `--cohort` asks it;
    - `pool map` fails a Mode A sheet only on an engine `error` reply, and `run_checks` is called only by `pack-audit` and the test-only pool sweep;
    - a CACHED map runs nothing at all.
    So two thin commands were added, both read-only:
    - `l7r-mode-a sweep <map>...` (`rust/mode_a/src/sweep.rs`): the pool sweep's `compose`, `with_context` and `judge` moved out of `#[cfg(test)] pool_sweep.rs`, which now calls them;
    - `hamlet --check <spec>...` (`rust/phases/src/spec_check.rs`, a new file and one `mod` line in `lib.rs`, so the T277 builder's `driver.rs` is untouched; the binary's arm is thin).
  - **Steps are the launcher's own commands** (`scripts/gates/l7r-gate.sh <words>`), run through a `Launch` trait, so the tests drive a fake and the line-coverage floor is met with no cargo or map in a test.
  - **Measured 2026-11-22, this clone, warm binaries, read-only (wall time of the make target or launcher command):**
    - **References.** Hamlet: `make hamlet SPEC=pool/hamlets/inashiro/inashiro.spec.json` 0.68 s and 0.43 s, measured 2026-11-22 (wall time, two runs); `l7r-gate.sh hamlet --check` on Inashiro 0.05 s warm and 5.6 s on its first, building, call, measured 2026-11-22 (wall time); Mode A: `make pack-audit` on one sheet 0.09 s, measured 2026-11-22 (wall time, two sheets twice each); `l7r-gate.sh mode-a sweep county-magistracy-example` 0.08 s warm and 16.3 s building, measured 2026-11-22 (wall time).
    - **Whole runs.** `make cohort` 4.4 s and 4.8 s, measured 2026-11-22 (wall time, two runs), and `l7r-gate.sh hamlet --cohort 1 48` in the tool profile 0.59 s, measured 2026-11-22 (wall time); `hamlet --check` of the five pool hamlets 0.15 s, measured 2026-11-22 (wall time); `make rust-test CRATE=rust/mode_a` 1.6 s with nothing moved, measured 2026-11-22 (wall time), and 29.9 s and 24.8 s fresh with 315 tests then, measured 2026-11-22 (wall time, `FRESH=1`, two runs).
    - **`pool map`.** Not timed: it rewrites tracked pool files when a map is not current, and two other builders were editing pool sheets and engine code in this clone.
  - **Counted cost.** Each run ends with its steps and rows: `make maps: <n> step(s) over <k> tier row(s), every one clean` (or `<m> failed: <labels>`). A reference run is two steps a row, one map drawn and one judged. A whole run is two steps for Mode A (every live map drawn, the crate's tests) and three for hamlets (every pool hamlet drawn, every one checked, the cohort's 48 seeds).
  - **Upkeep, no version** (constitution, Governance: "UPKEEP is no amendment and takes no version: ... a retired command name"):
    - VI's tier-table sentence names `make maps`' tier table at `rust/gate/crates/pool/src/maps.rs` where it named `mapcheck.py`;
    - T228's note on the 2.37.0 amendment says the clause was kept and the command rebuilt;
    - `docs/efficiency-tooling.md` (the refusal table's `make maps` row) and the make-docs section prose (`rust/gate/crates/cohort/src/make_docs.rs`, with `docs/make-targets.html` regenerated by `make docs`) name the command again;
    - the pair guard test's comment on `make maps`, whose assertion (no gate) stands.
    The 1.12.0 and 1.12.1 history entries keep their words.

### T252 Approach (checklist part A)

1. **The goal, in the world.** A session changing a generator types one command. It proves the change on the reference map first, at about half a second, and only then pays for the whole tier. The tool chooses the scope, so the session cannot choose it wrong.
2. **The constraints.** Constitution VI's clause (a single command whose scope follows the last run, one piece of state, `SCOPE=` overrides, a tier table with a named reference per tier); the GM's ruling of 2026-11-22; new Rust code owes 100% line coverage.

4. **Do they describe the world here?** Yes: the five pool hamlets, the two Mode A tiers with pool folders (`magistracies`, `country-shrines`), and the two named references, Inashiro and county-magistracy-example. Both references are held live by `the_real_table_names_live_maps_and_covers_every_tier`.
5. **The order.** After the batch landing at 65ede82bb6. Beside the T259/T277 builders (`rust/phases`: this task adds `spec_check.rs`, a `mod` line in `lib.rs` and the binary's arm, and leaves `driver.rs` alone) and the T275-T281 builders (`rust/mode_a/src/compound`, the sheets: this task touches neither).
6. **The exits.** Green: the tests of the pool, mode_a and phases crates green at the line-coverage floor and `make closing-checks T=T252 F=449` green. Red: what failed recorded and the task set down, a claim that it cannot be done ruled through `make arbiter-ask`.
7. **The search smell.** None.
8. **The budget.** One landing.
9. **Done, measured.** The tests above green at 100%, and the reference judges clean on the real tree (measured 2026-11-22). After the commit, `make maps SCOPE=reference` runs both references clean and a bare `make maps` after it goes wide.
10. **Before moving a constant.** n/a.
11. **Before fitting things into room.** n/a.
12. **Before any fix.** No map changes. The fix is the clause's own command, which was missing.

### T351, T352, T353, T354, T355, T356, T357, T359, T363, T364, T365, T366, T367, T368 Approach (checklist part A)

1. **The goal, in the world.** A county magistracy whose gatekeepers sit beside the gate they keep, whose tax-rice store stands
   smaller than the magistrate's house, whose junior samurai have a rowhouse to sleep in and whose cell stands in the court quarter
   rather than at the gate; an accused who kneels before the magistrate, not off to one side; an open workshop drawn open; an
   armory that may stand at either end of its hall; a hall that always has its dais; notes and claims that say what is drawn.
2. **The constraints.** Constitution XII, XIV and XVI; 0093 (the gatehouse beside the gate, the gate posts), 0096 (the cell in the
   court quarter), 0097 (junior officials' rowhouses on the grounds; a few men a dwelling), 0099 (the dais over the hearing court,
   the accused before it), 0101 (the privies), 0113 (the kakiyaku-beya's scribes), 0116 (the coverage band; a granary below the
   residence), 0123 (the armory's side varied; the granary at a flank column's head); room before packing; several attested forms a
   knob. **For MODE 4 (T367):** `rust/mode_a/src/audit/armory.rs` records the round arbiter's `ask:armory-store-ubame` route (a) as
   "one choice among the sites a sheet offers ... one choice, no nested roll" (its module claim and `rolled`'s), while T367 adds a
   second roll, `armory end bay` [west, east], taken only where the site roll gives the hall. The arbiter's words
   (specs/451-time-retro-and-efficiency/arbiter.jsonl): route (b) was refused because it "puts a nested roll and its 1-in-3 odds
   behind a guessed knob" turning a site into a store; route (a) "adds no new GUESS and no rule a source lacks". The end-bay roll
   chooses within the hall between two forms 0123 attests (Pingyao's west, Jiexiu's both and later the east, Zhenping's east and
   west), at even odds, and turns no site into another. The question: does the ruling's "no nested roll" reach a second knob of two
   attested forms under the hall site (then T367 needs the arbiter), or only route (b)'s guessed sub-roll among the sites (then the
   two claims want restating to say so)?
3. **Where each comes from.** R: the pages above and the research passes of 2026-11-22 (cell seat, junior lodging) and 2026-11-23
   (where the junior rowhouse stood and its dwelling's size: Sakai 1728, Sayama, Omori; whether a cell stood joined: SILENT, Naruto,
   Maruyama); O: the reviews' measurements, the drawn svg's rects, `make pack-audit`; G: none new.
4. **Do they describe the world here?** The junior rowhouse's form is attested for an intendant's office (0097); its seat is
   attested only at a town magistracy and a domain jin'ya (side or rear, apart from the gate) and SILENT for an intendancy, so the
   free run of the front wall, 57 ft west of the gate's post, is a GUESS; the dwelling 12 x 24 ft is Obata's 2-ken frontage at 0097's
   24 ft depth cap, above Sakai's doshin floor of about 216 sq ft (a GUESS); at most three men a dwelling is 0097's few, kept at or
   above the barracks' 88 sq ft a man by station (a GUESS); the servants' dwelling of 12 ft is a GUESS (no page sizes one; by station
   no wider than the foot soldier's). The cell's join is SILENT.
5. **The order.** Engine fixes red first; the sheets; `types.json`; docs and claims; notes last; `make map` and `make pack-audit` on
   the five, `make rust-test CRATE=rust/mode_a`; this section and its decision; the claims (triage, impl-drift); the Occasions lines,
   `make verify`, the map reviews; `make closing-checks`.
6. **The exits.** Green: pack-audit all OK on the five sheets, mode_a green, the claims IN-STEP, the reviews' NEEDS-WORK filed or
   fixed, `make closing-checks` green in the bundle's files. Red: what failed recorded and the task set down, a claim that it
   cannot be done ruled through `make arbiter-ask`.

### T377 (the round arbiter's `ask:glyph-occasions-emit-449-T351`, 2026-11-23, ruled a tool fault: 48 of the T351 bundle's 53 glyph-check units were owed on marks unchanged or only displaced, observed 2026-11-23, method: the review tree's main and clone svgs per data-kind, data-id stripped)

- **Approach**: In `rust/gate/crates/reviews/src/reviews/owed/redrawn.rs`, where the code cannot tell which kinds a change redraws (a kind chosen at run time, as in emit.rs `building`, or a line of the sheet's roll, compound.rs `sheet`), each compound map's drawing is now compared with its drawing at the base, kind by kind, in a new `owed/marks.rs`. Each token is attributed to its own `data-kind` or `data-part-of`, else to the enclosing element's; `data-id` is stripped; and a changed `<defs>` entry owes each kind that uses it, transitively. A kind is owed only where its marks differ, on the first map where they differ. The base text is the base commit's blob, else the mirror's copy, as `base_legends` reads it. The whole legend is still owed where the marks cannot be compared: the hamlet driver (its marks are not read by kind), a drawing not current, a drawing the base does not hold, or a difference that no kind owns. The occasion says which. What the code tells (a literal `data-kind` in a changed mark, or a writer method whose uses reach one) stays owed as before, and `the_compound_engines_marks_owe_their_kinds_on_the_compound` pins that: a writer method's edit owes the well, whose own mark writes through it, but not the hall, whose kind is chosen at run time and whose drawing is unchanged. The ruling's second half, "let the push read an arbiter accept as a glyph unit's discharge", is a new verb, `l7r-gate reviews discharge --root R --ruling TRIGGER UNIT...` (`owed/discharged.rs`; `make review-discharge RULING= UNITS=`). It records the ruling against each owed glyph unit, bound to the digest of that kind's marks now. The ruling must be an `accept` in some `specs/*/arbiter.jsonl`, and the record is all or none. `all_owed` drops a unit whose record's ruling still reads `accept` and whose kind's marks still have that digest, so the push (`review-gate.sh`), the checkpoint and `make verify` stop owing it, and `reviews owed --why` names each unit discharged. Before it writes anything, the verb refuses a ruling that is no accept, and a unit that is not owed now, is not a glyph check, or is on a map that draws no mark of its kind to bind to. It cannot tell which units the ruling discharged, because an `ask:` ruling names them only in its words, nor whether their marks are the ones the ruling measured, because it records no marks. So a push names only units the cited ruling discharged, by name or by a class the ruling states, and only where that kind's marks are unchanged between the drawing the ruling measured and the drawing being recorded, compared kind by kind with `data-id` stripped (the `marks.rs` rule), and states both, each unit matched to the ruling's words and the measurement with its date and method, in its own plan section. Each unit's record names the ruling it cites, so `reviews owed --why` shows every discharge's ruling for audit. A unit the ruling kept owed, or one an unrelated accept does not name, stays owed. Any unit whose marks differ stays owed, as the ruling asks: "If a sheet changes again before the push, any kind whose marks change is owed again under the rule." Once recorded, a discharge holds only while its kind's marks keep the recorded digest. The T351 bundle's landing carries its three arbiter rulings at its own push, so the unit list a discharge there would have named, which this section's two BLOCKED rounds were about, is moot and dropped here.

### T377 Approach (checklist part A)

1. **The goal, in the world.** A change to the Mode A compound's drawing code owes a glyph check only for a kind whose drawn marks changed, or that the code itself names. A round arbiter's accept stands for the units it ruled for as long as their marks stay as they were when it was recorded.

**Misses and false sends: the rule and the file**

- **The 147 forced claims** (docs/building-programs.md, two sections): round 2's `make claims-checked` stored each section's snapshot with a hand edit in two GENERATED table rows (the latrine and privy rows, which `make building-programs` writes from sheet/latrine.md's Guesses). Regeneration put the rows back to HEAD's words. The section core now differs from the snapshot, but `git diff` against origin/main no longer shows those lines, so `gather_section` and `gather_pages` (rust/gate/crates/claims/src/claims/triage.rs: `words.len() < missing.len()` forces a claim when a removed block's words cannot be shown, about lines 376-381 and 492-495) force every claim in both sections. Two rules meet here: a generated file's rows are claim-bearing text the claims index snapshots, and the triage can only show a removed block that git's history still holds. A revert, or any generated row rewritten back, forces a whole section to full impl-drift.
- **Stables' Depiction, the predicted miss (confirmed):** 0108.drawing's new GUESS `one-gable-door` is a pure addition (a new bold item), and sheet/stables.md's Depiction ("running its length with the door at its end") states no ABSENCE phrase, so `modal-triage` cleared `modal-depiction:sheet/stables` by the tool at the write stage, and again after the check session (whose rewrites of 0108's question page sent stables' Entry units, not its Depiction). The rule: the pop-up echo in rust/gate/crates/owed/src/triage/change.rs reads only sentences a page held and lost or rewrote, and `ABSENCE` matches only "the one case", "only one case" and "every plan"; a new block that bears on a pop-up's own statement reaches it only through those. The Depiction was fixed by hand (XIV), which owed its own depiction check.
- **The T400 miss** (`rust/mode_a/src/compound/emit.rs::grounds#office front, residence rear`): its index row's verdict was MISLABELED (the DEVIATION label T400 removes). `owed_one` (rust/gate/crates/claims/src/claims/index.rs, about line 611) owes a claim with changed code unless `relabeled_only` holds, and `relabeled_only` (same file, line 447) returns true for ANY claim whose row says `verdict: MISLABELED` once the unit's body is unchanged (`|| is(was, "verdict", "MISLABELED")`, 385 T23 D45: "a MISLABELED verdict answered by the relabel it prescribed"). A comment edit never changes the body, so a MISLABELED claim's account can be rewritten freely, not just relabeled, and nothing checks it. The restated account ("the residence behind the office, the yamen's order and Takayama's (one Japanese case)") went unchecked; the part it dropped (the inner court north) is the new CONVENTION claim, which is owed.

- **22 forced claims on the T378 residue** (docs/building-programs.md, Magistrate's manor section): each claim's own comment line differs from its index row's `code` only by T192's `#item` anchors (`GUESS <page>#<item>`; all 22 hunks anchor-only, checked by stripping `#[\w-]+`). `make claims-owed` owed none of them before the edit (its fingerprint does not count the anchor), but once the section's visible text moves, `gather_code` (rust/gate/crates/claims/src/claims/triage.rs, about lines 303-339) compares the row's `code` with the index's and forces every claim whose own line appears in an added hunk. The two readings of "did this claim's code move" disagree on T192's anchors, so a section triage of any section T192 relabeled forces its anchored claims.

### T415 (impl-drift 2026-11-24 read `row_shelter`'s `sheltered` form as a village shelter belt on a row settlement; the record says it is not one)

- **Approach**: no engine code changes; the claim is restated (constitution XIV: a wrong outcome, not a difference). `row_shelter`'s two forms are both groves, never a belt: `research/questions/0033-row-villages-resson.drawing.html` has each row village choose at even odds whether its leeward row, on a street with farms on both sides that runs across the wind, is drawn with full groves like the row across (`own_grove`) or after the farm the row across already shelters, its windward grove thin (`sheltered`), and labels the even odds a GUESS.
